articles.title_orig: As politicians argue about China, US patients find cutting-edge treatment there
articles.title_zh: As politicians argue about China, US patients find cutting-edge treatment there
articles.content_orig:
Until recently, a Manhattanite might venture no more than a few dozen blocks to find the world’s most sophisticated cancer treatment. Cutting-edge American medicines have helped reduce the U.S. cancer death rate by about a third since 1990, and New York City hospitals deliver some of the best care in the country.
But in January 2025, the city’s health systems had no good options for Debbie Doppelt, a 60-year-old jeweler with an unusual form of lung cancer that mostly afflicts nonsmokers like her. The Food and Drug Administration hadn’t yet approved sunvozertinib, a drug developed in China that targets the mutation driving Doppelt’s tumors. She had been through chemotherapy and surgery, but the cancer had now spread to her brain. And she didn’t qualify for the relevant clinical trials.
Then an option emerged, in an offhand remark.
“Too bad she’s not Chinese,” a doctor told her son Max Doppelt, who had organized his mother’s care since her 2023 diagnosis. “She could go to a pharmacy in China and buy it.”
Within hours, mother and son had reached out to friends and relatives, one of whom procured a small supply of sunvozertinib from a contact living in China. A few months later, Max flew to Shanghai to get a refill.
Other patients have followed. “No organization or doctor is guiding patients to China, but word gets out,” Max said. He said he knows of at least 30 Americans who’ve made the pilgrimage to obtain the drug, which the FDA licensed in July 2025 but wasn’t yet on the U.S. market as of mid-October of this year.
Sunvozertinib, made by Shanghai-based Dizal Pharmaceutical, isn’t the only treatment drawing patients to China. Americans, Europeans, and others are trekking there to enter clinical trials for CAR-T therapy, an area in which China is now a world leader .
China, until recently known more as a supplier of drug precursor chemicals and generic medicines, has become a biotech powerhouse, accounting for as much as 46% of new drugs tested around the world in 2025. U.S. pharmaceutical companies are testing new therapies there and signing billion-dollar contracts with Chinese firms to develop and market their drugs.
China’s progress has alarmed some politicians, who warn of lost jobs and U.S. dependency on Chinese medicines. The Trump administration in June kicked off Operation TrialBlazer, aimed at speeding up some FDA regulatory processes to lure back more clinical trials.
China’s poor showing in vaccine and drug development during the covid pandemic prompted the country to overhaul its biotech sector, dramatically altering the global industry, said Sam Rasty, a veteran of small biotech companies who now leads one called FynderBio. Venture capital now flows heavily to early-stage clinical work in China and Australia, where regulatory systems enable key first-in-human studies much more quickly than in the United States.
Chinese companies are so much faster at this process that U.S. biotechs, which used to share early advances at conferences or funding meetings, now routinely conceal their progress out of fear that competitors will take their ideas and speed them to market, said Steve Potts, CEO of Breakthru Medicine, a small biotech.
At a meeting he attended in May, nearly all the 60 biotech CEOs in the room planned to run phase 1 trials in Australia, Europe, or China, Potts said. Five or 10 years ago, most of those trials would have been carried out in the U.S.
“Slow and prohibitive” FDA requirements are driving investment to more-nimble Chinese companies, President Donald Trump’s nominee to lead the agency, Heidi Overton, warned in her opening statement at her Sept. 24 confirmation hearing.
The movement of clinical trials overseas “should give pause to every American and those who serve on their behalf,” Overton said. “When we lose this advantage, we lose our health security. And when we lose our health security, we lose everything.”
Overton pledged to continue TrialBlazer, which mirrors Australian processes begun in 1991. It is aimed at accelerating clinical trials and approvals so patients do not feel compelled to seek treatment abroad, said Department of Health and Human Services spokesperson Emily Hilliard. It is sometimes legal to obtain medication abroad for personal use, but the FDA “cautions patients about potential safety and quality risks associated with treatments outside our regulatory system,” she added.
As the FDA moves to streamline drug development, members of Congress are trying to slow Chinese firms’ integration into U.S. biotech.
Rep. John Moolenaar (R-Mich.), who chairs the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, in June co-sponsored legislation with Rep. Debbie Dingell (D-Mich.) requiring all U.S. pharmaceutical deals with Chinese companies to be cleared by the Treasury Department.
Others see biotech protectionism as misguided. China’s focus on improved medicines can only help us, said Peter Kolchinsky, managing partner of RA Capital Management, which has Chinese investments in its biotech portfolio.
“We may be adversaries in many areas, but we’re not competing with them to cure cancer. We are collaborating with them to cure cancer,” he said. “There are things that are bigger enemies than any other nation on Earth.”
A minor but persistent cough led to the diagnosis of Debbie Doppelt’s cancer in late 2023. Chemo, immunotherapy, and surgery kept it at bay for months, but in December 2024, scans showed the cancer had spread to her brain, with 10 tiny tumors.
The FDA earlier that year had approved amivantamab, a drug that targeted the mutation driving Doppelt’s tumor, but Max was concerned about its toxicity. Also, several doctors he consulted told him that amivantamab might not penetrate brain tissue to fight cancer there.
Doppelt tried to enter a clinical trial at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, where she was a patient, for zipalertinib, another drug that targeted her mutation. But in January 2025, the Doppelts learned that a slight scarring on her lungs had rendered her ineligible for the study.
That left sunvozertinib, which gained approval in China in 2023. It was also being tested in the U.S., but only in late-stage trials in which half the subjects received chemotherapy only. That risk was a nonstarter for Doppelt, whose cancer had already outsmarted chemo.
So Max flew to Shanghai, returning with 26 boxes of sunvozertinib in his luggage. The drugs cost about $10,000, he said.
“Getting on the plane and bringing the medicine home felt like my life’s purpose,” Max said. “The data was so clear that this drug had significant efficacy in the brain. Anything else she might do, she might not last a year.”
On Sept. 1 of this year, AstraZeneca signed an agreement with Dizal to distribute the drug worldwide, and it plans to make it available in the U.S. by the start of 2027, spokesperson Tara Parsell said.
Doppelt, who runs a diamond business with her husband, has tried to stay positive and healthy, scarcely missing a day of work since her 2023 diagnosis. She said she’s grateful she has a loving community and the means to afford the best available therapies.
“I think I’ve been pretty successful at having, actually, an amazing three years,” she said. “In some ways a better three years, with all of it, than the three years before, because you’re so appreciative of everything.”
Doppelt’s parents were Holocaust survivors. “They were always saying: ‘This piece of bread tastes so good! Do you know what it is to be hungry?’”
Searching for help for his mother gave Max, a 30-year-old computer engineer, an idea for helping patients find the right treatment — which, in cases of advanced cancers, may be a clinical trial.
A year ago, he quit his tech job and started a company that uses artificial intelligence to combine data from research and drug company sites with a patient’s health records to help them find the right study.

articles.title_orig: Russia, Ukraine agree to ceasefire in Ukrainian city hit by food crisis, brokered by Melania Trump
articles.title_zh: Russia, Ukraine agree to ceasefire in Ukrainian city hit by food crisis, brokered by Melania Trump
articles.content_orig:
People in Russian-occupied city facing severe shortages of food, water and electricity, with some reportedly surviving on weeds
The White House has said that Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a ceasefire in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, where a deepening humanitarian crisis has left thousands of civilians struggling to survive.
In a statement on Friday, the White House said both sides had agreed to halt all military operations in the city from 29 October to allow humanitarian aid deliveries and preparations for the evacuation of civilians.
Residents of the southern Ukrainian city, which has been under Russian occupation since February 2022, have described increasingly desperate conditions amid severe shortages of food, water and electricity. An estimated 2,000 people remain in the city, with some reportedly forced to survive on weeds, boiled grass, bread and meagre rations.
Both Russian and Ukrainian officials said all sides were close to agreeing to a ceasefire.
The White House statement said the ceasefire was brokered by Melania Trump , and her representative worked directly with ​Russian and Ukrainian ‌leadership to define the ​terms. “Residents who wish to evacuate will receive coordinated support and transportation to their preferred destination. I anticipate some will want to go to Russia, and some to Ukraine,” the first lady said.
Despite the claim the ceasefire had been brokered by Melania Trump, there had already been protracted efforts to organise a humanitarian ceasefire, with claims by Ukrainian officials that it had been Russia that had rejected previous calls.
Calls for a ceasefire had been issued by Pope Leo XIV – who discussed the issue with the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy – the United Nations, EU officials and the Council of Europe . As recently as 18 October, Ukraine’s ombudsman, Dmytro Lubinets, had also said he thought agreement was close without any mention of the first lady’s involvement.
Ukraine has for weeks been pushing for a civilian evacuation from Oleshky and nearby settlements, at times using drones to airdrop emergency food and medical supplies into town.
Meanwhile, Ukrainian forces continue to report widespread disruptions to the Starlink satellite network , despite Donald Trump’s claim that Elon Musk had lifted restrictions on the service.
The slowdown, which has affected the communications system used by Ukrainian troops, began last week after Trump and Elon Musk, the founder of Starlink, publicly criticised Zelenskyy over continued strikes on Russian oil refineries.
The restrictions have raised questions and confusion about who ordered the slowdown and why, with Trump and Musk denying responsibility. Asked about the Starlink slowdowns on Friday, Trump said he would speak to Musk if the restrictions remained in place.
“I’ve heard it was fixed, but if it’s not, I’ll speak to him,” he told reporters.
Ukrainian officials said throughout the day on Friday that speeds remained capped at about 100mph, with no indication that the restrictions had been lifted.
“At present, we have not observed any lifting of the restrictions on Starlink,” said Serhii Beskrestnov, a military expert who advises Zelenskyy.
“There have been isolated cases in which Starlink has operated at speeds slightly above the imposed limits, but this is likely due to SpaceX’s algorithms or specific conditions of use, rather than any lifting of the restrictions,” Beskrestnov added.
The speed restrictions have prevented Ukrainian military equipment, including drones, from maintaining a connection to the satellite network when travelling at high speeds, hampering offensive drone operations and efforts to intercept incoming Russian attacks.
after newsletter promotion
The slowing down of Starlink, coupled with Zelenskyy’s complaints that Washington had temporarily suspended intelligence-sharing with Kyiv, has plunged relations between Ukraine and the US to a new low in recent days.
Tensions first flared after Washington’s surprise decision to lift sanctions on Russia and begin importing Russian diesel , as Trump sought to bring down US energy prices before the midterm elections. Maritime tracking data showed that the first tanker carrying Russian diesel was en route to New York on Thursday.
Meanwhile, Russia launched another overnight barrage against Ukraine, even as Moscow said a fresh round of US-brokered talks aimed at ending the war could take place next month.
The Kremlin spokesperson, Dmitry Peskov, said on Friday that trilateral talks between Russia, Ukraine and the US were expected to resume in Abu Dhabi in November. Previous rounds of negotiations have failed to produce a breakthrough, with Moscow and Kyiv far away over the terms of any peace settlement.
Among Russia’s maximalist demands are that Ukraine withdraw its forces from territory it still controls in the east of the country, drastically reduce the size of its military and adopt a neutral status that would rule out Nato membership.
Speaking to a Russian state television reporter late on Thursday, Putin once again questioned Ukraine’s sovereignty, echoing claims he has repeatedly made throughout the war. “The lands lost by Kyiv are not their territory, they are Russia’s historical lands,” Putin said.
The Russian president also cited unspecified genetic research to revive his longstanding claim that Russians and Ukrainians were “one people”, before insisting that Moscow would achieve all the objectives of its full-scale invasion.

articles.title_orig: Netanyahu vows West Bank military operation after attack kills two Israeli soldiers
articles.title_zh: Netanyahu vows West Bank military operation after attack kills two Israeli soldiers
articles.content_orig:
Diggers were seen demolishing Palestinian homes on Friday afternoon
The Israeli military has begun demolishing Palestinian buildings in the city of Hebron, after two Israeli soldiers were killed in an attack by two Palestinian gunmen.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the military would "destroy" the neighbourhood where the two attackers came from, and that Israel was ready for "extensive action" in the occupied West Bank.
Three other soldiers were wounded in the attack at a checkpoint outside Hebron, before the gunmen were shot dead, officials say.
It comes at a time of high tensions, with extremist Jewish settlers targeting Palestinians during the annual olive harvest, and Israel's general election taking place in four days' time.
Footage verified by the BBC shows an intense gun battle between soldiers and the gunmen. Other footage shows two gunmen exit a car armed with what appears to be a handgun and an assault rifle and start firing on soldiers at the checkpoint, before coming under return fire.
Photos of one of the suspected attackers were shared by AFP news agency
The incident has already begun to influence the ongoing election campaign, with Netanyahu - who has built his campaign on the promise of security - saying that his Likud party would cancel campaign events which had been set for Friday morning.
Speaking later from the scene, Netanyahu said that the military would "demolish this place and completely transform it," referring to the Hebron neighbourhood where the attackers are said to have come from.
It is common for Israeli forces to demolish the homes of Palestinians who are suspected of carrying out attacks on Israelis - a practice Israeli rights groups have criticised as collective punishment.
Netanyahu likened his plans to previous operations in West Bank refugee camps where residential buildings were demolished and thousands were displaced.
He also said he had reviewed plans for the largest military operation in the West Bank in decades - though did not say when it could be carried out.
He added that he had imposed cordons around the city of Hebron - which has around 200,000 residents - and the nearby city of Halhul.
Netanyahu's far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich called for Israel to launch a campaign in the West Bank "exactly like in Gaza or Lebanon," while far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir called for Israel to dismantle the Palestinian Authority.
On Thursday, Foreign Minister Israel Katz accused opposition leaders of undermining the government by criticising Netanyahu's warnings of an attack ahead of the election, saying they would be "responsible" for any future attack on the country.
Opposition chiefs, including frontrunner Gadi Eisenkot and former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, offered their condolences to the families of the killed troops and praised those who killed the attackers.
The Israeli military said it had found a large quantity of ammunition in the attackers' vehicle, and that they believe the gunmen had intended to carry out a much larger attack on the nearby Route 35, but ran into the checkpoint - so instead decided to open fire there.
At least 96 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli forces or settlers in the West Bank since the start of the year, according to the UN.
Four Israelis, both security forces and civilians, have been killed by Palestinians there over the same period, the UN says - not including those killed in Friday's attack.

articles.title_orig: Leaked trove reveals extent of far-right AfD’s efforts to court Trump and Maga allies
articles.title_zh: Leaked trove reveals extent of far-right AfD’s efforts to court Trump and Maga allies
articles.content_orig:
Despite distraction and distortion, voters know what issues will be informing their votes in this election
This was originally published in The Stakes 2026, a newsletter about the midterm elections. Sign up to get it in your inbox
Elections too often get pigeonholed. The hot take, or simplistic analysis, would have it that just one issue – often the issue the source so happens to be most animated about – will decide the entire result.
Tens of millions of Americans will go to the polls next month. Will they be galvanized by affordability? Maybe it’s Iran. Or healthcare? Taxes, perhaps. Or crime.
It depends, of course, on whom you ask. The US electorate is not a monolith. Just as different voters are grappling with different pressures and realities, they have different priorities and concerns.
Take a look at our voter panel . For Justin Daniels, 45, in Detroit, Michigan, the most significant issue in this election is economic malaise. For Yajaira Martinez, 43, in Pharr, Texas, it’s labor. For Scott Akridge, 60, in Marietta, Georgia, it’s the administration’s brutal crackdown on immigration.
The challenge for any one party trying to win over such a sprawling country is whether it can address enough of these concerns, and obtain the trust of enough voters, to build a coalition.
Which makes the latest polling all the more disconcerting for Republicans , less than two weeks before election day.
The headline takeaways from the most recent Washington Post-ABC News-Ipsos survey were damning enough: as my colleague Shrai Popat reported , most Americans think Donald Trump is using the US presidency to enrich himself, and his approval rating has fallen to a new low.
Beneath the surface, though, the numbers are yet more dismal for Republicans.
Presented with a dozen issues, from affordability and corruption to taxes and transgender issues, respondents were asked which of the two main parties they trust to do a better job of handling them. On all but one – crime – a greater share picked Democrats than Republicans.
On the economy, as the White House continues to hail a “new golden age”, Republicans have lost ground significantly over the past six months. While they commanded a one-point lead over Democrats in April, they are now nine points behind on the issue voters consistently rank as a top concern.
And on immigration, which Trump and his officials have put at the heart of his second presidency, the five-point Republican lead in April has reversed. Almost two years into the administration’s deadly and controversial crackdown, Democrats are now ahead by two points.
In Kansas, where voters have not sent a Democrat to the US Senate since 1932, the party’s candidate, Adam Hamilton, has been pledging to turn down the heat , and ignore partisan battles, amid rising political polarization. Some recent polls have put him ahead.
Midterm elections are almost always tough for Washington’s governing party. There is a conventional playbook for navigating this: senior figures fan out nationwide to reassure the people who backed them two years prior that they get it. They hear them. They’re on it. They just need more time.
The president is indeed fanning out across the country. This week alone, he was in Kansas on Monday and North Carolina on Tuesday, before South Carolina on Wednesday, Iowa on Thursday and Florida on Friday. Georgia and Michigan follow this weekend. JD Vance is on a cross-country tour of his own.
But this is where Trump and his allies depart from convention. Rather than acknowledge the golden age has yet to shine for much of the country – let alone concede that some of his priorities since taking office, like the beautification of Washington, or adding his name to the Kennedy Center, were not among the campaign promises his base had found so appealing in 2024 – Trump has opted for an altogether different response.
He has tried to change the subject.
This summer, as questions over Iran, the cost of living and hardline anti-immigration policies loomed large, the most powerful elected officials in the US tried to stoke fears that communism was rife inside the Democratic party.
In September, the president dangled a $5,000 “Trump dividend” for every US citizen, a proposal that was widely criticized as a pre-election bribe.
Now, in the final stretch of the campaign, those questions very much remain. Rather than address them, Republicans appear to be resorting to a volatile mix of distraction and distortion.
Having spent much of the Iran war, which he launched in February, claiming it was about to end, the president is now pivoting to Ukraine – striking a stunning deal to buy Russian diesel , pausing some sanctions on Moscow and suggesting the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, should quit.
after newsletter promotion
And as France was gripped by fresh unrest this weekend, Vance entered the chat. Demonstrations that began as student protests against crumbling schools and the soaring cost of living were, in fact, evidence of “western liberals” having “imported the third world” into their countries, according to the vice-president.
“And I hope Americans are paying attention. This is the future congressional Democrats seek for your country,” added Vance. Not to be outdone, Trump himself has used public appearances to echo such warnings in recent days, as my colleagues Joseph Gedeon and David Smith reported.
Many Americans are paying close attention – not to France, necessarily, but to the issues that dominate their daily lives. In November, we’ll find out whom Americans trust to address them.
The US politics team hosted a series of reader Q&As leading up to the midterms. In our final session, Guardian immigration reporters answered your questions about how ICE and Trump’s mass deportation agenda could shape election results. See our other conversations here:

Mary Peltola’s campaign to represent Alaska in the US Senate has taken her to parts of the huge state’s interior that are inaccessible by road and on the frontlines of the cost-of-living crisis she hopes will make her the first Democrat to win the seat in nearly two decades.
She has been to towns where paper towels retail for $40, a half gallon of oat milk goes for $21 and the cost of a new freezer can be quadruple what it is in the state’s largest city, Anchorage, simply because it’s so complicated to get there. She’s heard of communities along the Arctic Ocean where power bills have climbed to $1,500 a month because they rely on generators for power and the Iran war has pushed the cost of diesel to new heights.
“Nobody can afford that,” Peltola said in an interview.

articles.title_orig: Chart: A record two-thirds of car sales in China are now electric vehicles
articles.title_zh: Chart: A record two-thirds of car sales in China are now electric vehicles
articles.content_orig:
For the first time, new-energy vehicles (NEVs) made up 67% of new car sales in China in September, according to the latest data from the China Passenger Car Association (CPCA).
The figures show that NEVs, which include battery electric cars and plug-in hybrids, captured a record share of sales, even though fewer were sold than last year.
This is because sales of combustion-engine cars are falling steeply, a trend that the CPCA has attributed to rising petrol prices following the start of the Hormuz crisis .
Indeed, sales of fuel-only cars were down 31% year-on-year in the first nine months of 2026, with plug-in hybrid sales down 26% – whereas battery EV sales were only down 4%.
One analyst tells Carbon Brief that China’s rapidly growing EV fleet has offset demand for 143m barrels of oil since the start of the Hormuz crisis.
Another says that the crisis is “reinforcing China’s electrification of road transport”.
Meanwhile, amid slowing domestic sales, Chinese carmakers’ exports of NEVs more than doubled [in 2026 to date / in September] from a year earlier.
A record two out of every three cars sold in September in China were NEVs, according to CPCA data, as shown in the figure below.
(NEVs predominantly include battery electric vehicles – BEVs – and plug-in hybrids  – PHEVs. BEVs only run on electricity, whereas PHEVs also have a combustion engine.)
This marks a rapid rise for NEVs from just 6% of new car sales in 2020 up to 58% in 2026 to date – and a record 67% in the month of September.
This year, NEVs’ share of sales has also bounced back from a low of 39% in January, after the full purchase tax exemption that had been in place for more than a decade came to an end in December 2025.
The gain in NEV share in 2026 has come amid a slowdown across the wider domestic passenger-car market, which has hit sales of combustion-engine vehicles particularly hard.
This September, passenger-car retail sales across all categories declined, with overall sales volumes falling 28% year-on-year.
The contraction was led by combustion-engine vehicles, which saw sales fall 43% year-on-year in September and 31% in 2026 to date.
However, sales of PHEVs also fell by 36% year-on-year in September and by 26% in 2026 to date. By comparison, BEVs performed better, although sales still declined 8.5% from a year earlier in September and 4% in 2026 to date.
As a result, NEV sales overall fell by 17% in September and 13% in 2026 to date.
While the market changes in 2026 to date were particularly dramatic, they reflect a broad continuation of trends seen over the past decade.
Indeed, sales of combustion-engine cars in China peaked in 2017 and they have been declining ever since, shown in the figure below.
Part of the reason for the advance of NEVs in 2026, said Chinese technology news outlet OFweek , was petrol cars “giving up market share” as they were outperformed by electric alternatives.
Cui Dongshu, secretary-general of the CPCA, cited higher petrol prices as an explanation for September’s weak combustion-car sales, in comments to financial news outlet National Business Daily .
Imports of oil into China in January-September have fallen 15% compared to 2025, equivalent to 470m barrels, as ongoing conflict tightened supply and drove up prices.
China’s passenger-car NEV fleet has displaced 143m barrels of oil so far during the strait of Hormuz crisis, Euan Graham , senior energy analyst at thinktank Ember , tells Carbon Brief.
EVs “accounted for 12% of the decrease in China’s oil use post-Hormuz”, according to an estimate provided to thinktank the Brookings Institute by an unnamed analyst.
Erica Downs , a senior research scholar at Columbia University’s Center on Global Energy Policy , tells Carbon Brief that the strait of Hormuz crisis and higher oil prices are “reinforcing China’s electrification of road transport”.
She says the “world’s largest oil supply disruption” vindicates China’s early bet on EVs, which was partly driven by concerns about oil-supply security.
Nevertheless, NEV sales have fallen year-on-year, albeit at a slower rate than overall car sales. The growth in NEV market share has also been decelerating.
Zhang Yichao , a partner at consulting firm AlixPartners , tells Carbon Brief that NEVs benefit from government trade-in policies and a “strong pipeline” of new models, particularly those involving innovation.
He says these factors help explain why NEVs sales have fallen at a slower rate to their combustion-car counterparts.
Cui told the state-run China National Radio that the fall for NEVs and for cars overall in September 2026, is also due to a high baseline of sales from the same month in 2025, as well as changes to trade-in policies and disruptions from the holiday period.
Other factors, says consulting firm Wood Mackenzie , are the weakened demand due to “demand pull-forward” in 2025 caused by the end of subsidies, as well as “tighter financing conditions”.
Zhang tells Carbon Brief he does not “see much more room ahead” for further growth in NEVs’ market share.
He adds that, in his view, their share in China is unlikely to exceed 80%, as some premium-market segments and specific use cases will continue to require combustion-engine vehicles.
Meanwhile, while domestic NEV retail sales fell 17% in September 2026, exports more than doubled, increasing 164% year-on-year, according to the CPCA .
This extends the decline in domestic sales and very strong growth in exports seen across 2026 to date, as shown in the figure below.
In September, 1,084,000 NEVs were sold domestically in China, while 558,000 NEVs were exported.
Exports are becoming increasingly important to Chinese carmakers, in the face of weaker domestic demand and cut-throat industrial competition.
The CPCA says exports have become “a core priority” for some carmakers.
However, the surge in exports from China has created concern in the EU, which has placed tariffs on imports of EVs from China and recently agreed plans to cut imports of hybrids.
Countries including Mexico and Turkey have also placed tariffs on Chinese EV imports.
At the same time, the Chinese government is putting policies in place that might be expected to disincentivise exports, such as cutting VAT export rebates.
Analysts differ on what impact this policy shift will have, with some saying it will be limited, while others believe it could cause the price of exported cars to rise.

articles.title_orig: Many feared trapped as a tall building collapses in Kenya
articles.title_zh: Many feared trapped as a tall building collapses in Kenya
articles.content_orig:
A multi-story building has collapsed in a busy commercial area of Kenya’s capital, and many people could be trapped beneath the rubble
NAIROBI, Kenya -- Many people were feared trapped as a tall building collapsed Friday in Kenya’s capital, leaving a huge mound of concrete and more than a dozen floors stacked like pancakes, with little space between them.
The building was under construction when it collapsed at about 1 p.m. along a busy commercial street in Nairobi's Eastleigh area, which is often crowded with thousands of traders and residents.
Nairobi police chief Issa Mohamud said the building had more than 10 upper floors under construction. Rescue operations were complicated, with police firing tear gas at people who had begun looting neighboring shops, as officers sought to clear the area and provide access to emergency response teams.
The Kenya Red Cross said its teams were on their way and urged people at the site to give responders space to work safely.
There was little in the way of heavy equipment immediately available. Hours later, a group of rescuers in hard hats were using poles stripped from trees to poke at the huge pile of rubble.
One excavator arrived on site and started moving the concrete bound with steel away so that the rescuers might reach the ground-level and basement floors that were said to have been rented out as shops while construction continued on the upper floors.
Residents said some of their loved ones who were trapped had made phone calls calling for help immediately after the collapse, but that their phones later became unreachable.
Building collapses are a recurring problem in Nairobi. County officials responsible for issuing building permits have been accused of failing to conduct adequate inspections to ensure developers comply with safety guidelines and construction standards.

articles.title_orig: AI-discovered bugs may soon trigger fresh disruptions, cyber experts say
articles.title_zh: AI-discovered bugs may soon trigger fresh disruptions, cyber experts say
articles.content_orig:
Cybersecurity teams around the globe are rushing to patch PHP programming language flaws this week, in an artificial intelligence safety moment that's being described as "Black October."
Nearly 70% of all websites use PHP, according to some estimates.
"In the last 2 days there have been several dozen cyber attacks which, in isolation, would each have been the worst to happen in an entire calendar year," John Milinovich, senior director of product management at Figma, wrote in a post on X on Thursday. "Every sector from government to education to big tech and banks is being massively affected, and people are starting to freak out."
Researchers at Google's Wiz and the AI firm Calif discovered major vulnerabilities in PHP in August by using advanced AI models from OpenAI and Google. But by Tuesday, the warnings had spread online, prompting governments and businesses around the globe to scramble to contain the fallout .
Major AI companies have been warning about the technology's advancing cybersecurity capabilities since April, when Anthropic announced a limited rollout of its powerful model called Mythos . Concerns mounted in July, when OpenAI disclosed that two of its models escaped containment, accessed the open internet and breached a company called Hugging Face .
Experts believe the PHP security flaws serve as the latest example of what's to come.
Jason Clinton, deputy chief information security officer at Anthropic, wrote in a post on X on Thursday that the cybersecurity landscape is likely to get "a lot worse" before it gets better.
"Security leaders, never let a crisis go to waste: please go to your boards and ask for help right now," Clinton said. "Not for ai, for the basics. (we need to hold on for ~18 months.)"
While many large companies have access to advanced models that they can use to harden their systems, serious bugs could be more challenging for small- and medium-sized businesses to address, Chris Krebs, former director of the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, told CNBC on Friday. He encouraged smaller companies to "constantly" scan for vulnerabilities, deploy patches as fast as possible or take legacy systems offline.
"This is a significant week or two in cybersecurity," Krebs told CNBC's "Squawk Box." "As I mentioned, 3% of all critical vulnerabilities ever discovered have been found in the last month."
Figma's Milinovich encouraged individuals to set up two-factor authentication for "everything," use a password manager, set up an identity protection app and move smart devices to their own network. He added that people should lean in and experiment with AI to understand how powerful the tools have become.
"While I still firmly believe that AI will be a net positive for humanity, it's more clear to me than ever that the societal and individual risk is very real, and is playing out NOW," Milinovich said.
Krebs added that company leaders and employees should check in on their security teams.
"Make sure they're doing okay," he said. "They've had a heck of a week."
—CNBC's Isabel O’Brien contributed to this report

articles.title_orig: The young Americans choosing Y2K cars over shiny new SUVs: ‘I get so much crap from people’
articles.title_zh: The young Americans choosing Y2K cars over shiny new SUVs: ‘I get so much crap from people’
articles.content_orig:
People under 35 are hunting for no-frills rides they can pay for in cash and fix themselves – defying expectations to take on steep loans
J ack Price joined the marines in fall 2021 knowing he would need a car to get around base and that he couldn’t afford a new one. A joyless, month-long search through dealer classifieds and Facebook Marketplace listings ended when his mother spotted a 2010 Volkswagen Jetta posted on her office listserv by a co-worker moving abroad. With just 60,000 miles (96,560km) on the meter, the car (a manual!) was mechanically sound, and the air conditioning, sunroof and Bluetooth radio worked too. At $6,000, it was a steal. Price paid in cash.
Five years on, the Jetta, which he called the Pewter Pebble, is still carting him from A to B in unassuming style. “I’ve completely driven it into the ground,” says the 30-year-old, who lives in Los Angeles. “All over bases, cross-country a couple times, not really lovingly. I get so much crap from people, but not people my age.”
For generations, buying a first new car has been a rite of passage in the US, the clearest sign of a young person responsibly striking out on their own. But younger millennials and gen Z are increasingly finding that path blocked. The average new vehicle costs more than $50,000, an alarming figure that reflects Americans’ insatiable appetite for progressively larger SUVs and pickups. Meanwhile, adults under 35 are disappearing from showroom floors, accounting for less than 10% of new vehicle registrations in 2024 – a new low.
According to the credit reporting agency Experian, the average monthly car payment in the US is $765 for a new car and $542 for a used one, with the loan terms now stretching to six, even seven, years. A record 21% of new-car buyers pay $1,000 or more a month , according to the autos research group Edmunds. And that’s before factoring in maintenance, fluctuating gas prices and the eye-watering insurance premiums often charged to drivers under 35.
For many young Americans already under the strain of student loans, high housing costs and an unforgiving labor market, buying a new car or even a newer used one is out of the question. Enter the Y2K car – the retro ride that has become a trendy romantic choice for some younger Americans. “There’s definitely a golden era of cars from the late 90s and early 2000s that people just really want all of a sudden,” says Charlie Spears, a service adviser at an independently owned repair shop in Atlanta who conducts prepurchase inspections of used cars on demand. “A lot of people just want something that’s not going to fail them.”
Y2K cars don’t encompass everything produced in that era. They are the ones that simply won’t die. Think wedge-shaped Honda Accords and slab-sided Toyota Camrys: dependable, hand-me-down transport that can last 150,000 miles or more with routine maintenance. (Price’s Jetta, which was built at the end of a model production run that began in 2005, just makes the cut.) They’re economical to run and relatively inexpensive to insure, owing to their drastically lower worth. Best of all, the purchase price is low enough to pay in cash. Even when buyers need a loan – at steep interest rates as modern cars have in effect become mortgage payments on wheels – they can pay it off in a fraction of the time it takes to finance a newer car.
The supply of these bargains is dwindling: used vehicles priced under $15,000, the sweet spot for Y2K cars, have shrunk from 21% of inventory a year ago to 15% , according to industry analysis from Cox Automotive – numbers that speak to the demand for affordable cars. “Part of the draw is the nostalgia factor – people wanting cars they grew up with,” says Consumer Reports’ autos expert Keith Barry. “An old car with the right music on is kind of the closest thing to a time machine.”
On social media, the Y2K car has emerged as an ironic status symbol – a marker of maturity, grit and lack of pretense. Defects – busted aircon, glitchy windows, bits and bobs that have failed, fallen off or been held on with gaffer tape – are simply treated as part of a Y2K car’s personality. “I don’t know what kind of disease that is in the brain,” says one TikTok creator, who has to pry open the fuel door of her 2003 Mitsubishi Outlander with a screwdriver . “But I don’t get frustrated. I’m like, ‘Oh, this is fun.’”
In a Y2K car that takes a lickin’ and keeps on tickin’, creature comforts are beside the point. For many, part of the appeal is the absence of dashboard infotainment displays and other screens that have replaced basic switches and knobs in newer cars, often in the name of cost-cutting. Automakers’ zeal to monetize in-car technology, sometimes charging extra to activate physically installed features such as heated seats and remote start, only reinforces young buyers’ doubts about the value of a new car.
At the same time, do-it-yourself repairs have become harder as cars grow more digitally complex and auto manufacturers cut off access to owners and even independent mechanics . Oftentimes, they require investing in specialty digital readers or computer software to diagnose problems, and bespoke tools for wrenching. Most car owners would sooner punt, take the car to the dealership and pay whatever the maintenance and repair costs – which, of course, is exactly the vertical integration that shareholder-bound manufacturers are after.
Hence the romance with Y2K cars: you can fix ’em yourself, their old-school controls fall easily to hand, they’re tried and tested, seemingly built to last. They just have an aura of invincibility – never mind that their age makes them fundamentally more dangerous and susceptible to frequent repairs. “I’ve used my Jetta as if it were a truck,” Price says. “Transported trees in it, put my surfboard through the sunroof. I’ve done every single thing possible to thrash it beyond its abilities.”
Price’s passengers, however, don’t have much appreciation for Pewter Pebble’s quirks. Often while carpooling to US military installations, senior officers compelled to hold up the sagging headliner would ask him when he was trading in his beater for a new truck or SUV. It was a similar story when Price left the military last year and started chauffeuring Alex Vindman, the Iraq war veteran turned US Senate hopeful, on the campaign trail during Florida’s special election. “I drove him around a couple times in it, and he was like, ‘ What is going on?’” Price says. “The fact that we expect folks who are getting paid, like, a grand a month to have a new car is nuts.”
T wenty-five miles north-west of downtown Atlanta, a half hour’s drive in optimistic traffic, sits Town Center at Cobb, a typical suburban mall in recession. But on the first Sunday of every month, the mall parking comes alive for Caffeine and Octane, a sprawling car show that’s open to the public, free to attend and also has long lines for coffee and donut trucks. And even though the usual turnout of 2,000-plus cars was winnowed down to a few hundred on the gray, showery morning of October’s show, it was still an impressive array of vintage American muscle, Japanese domestic market (or JDM) unicorns and multimillion-dollar exotics. The Y2K cars stood out, too.
Sitting right at the entrance of the show was Anthony DeNaples’s 2000 Buick Regal GS, a sleeper sedan that has become a cult classic. He bought it four months ago for $18,000 on Facebook Marketplace, a price he considered a bargain for such a rare commuter. “Person didn’t really know what they had,” says the 37-year-old custom car builder, who uses the car to ferry his two young daughters. His oldest is constantly goading him to do burnouts, which she calls “making stripes”. Modern cars, he reasons, have become so laden with safety systems – for keeping the car in lane, or slamming on the brakes when sensors detect an obstacle – that they’re less fun to drive hard. “A lot of newer cars, if you want to drive it how it’s meant to be driven,

articles.title_orig: US designates helium as a critical material, citing its importance for semiconductors
articles.title_zh: US designates helium as a critical material, citing its importance for semiconductors
articles.content_orig:
Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged in Please refresh your browser to be logged in
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
Helium producers in the United States will gain access to more federal financing and the government will keep a closer watch on the gas after the Energy Department designated it a critical material on Friday.
The Energy Department said the designation was made because helium is indispensable for making semiconductors that are essential to energy generation, and because the global supply is at risk of disruption.
Energy Secretary Chris Wright said the Trump administration is freeing America from reliance on foreign sources of critical materials, strengthening domestic manufacturing, supporting American jobs and securing the materials essential to U.S. economic and national security.
“President Trump is bringing back America’s manufacturing industry, and that means making sure we have the materials needed to build things in America again,” Wright said in a statement.
Helium is the 20th critical material identified by the department. Metallurgical coal used for steelmaking was the last substance to be added to the list, in 2025. Fluorine is the only other gas on it.
To qualify, a non-fuel mineral element or substance must serve an essential function in one or more energy technologies, and there must be a high risk of disruption to the supply chain.
The designation matters for reasons that go well beyond party balloons, even though helium is what makes them rise. The department points to the gas's role in wind, solar and nuclear energy production, space exploration, medical imaging and research.
Assistant Secretary of Energy Audrey Robertson said helium's unique properties make it irreplaceable, citing the facts that it is non-combustible and has the lowest boiling point of any gas. Robertson, who oversees the Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation, added that the nation needs an ample supply for semiconductors, quantum and super computing, and superconducting magnets.
“We need to make sure that we can build those here. And helium is one of those components that could be a single point of failure, where we cannot let that happen. That’s why we’re designating it within our statutory authority, but I think why it’s important is not necessarily for our birthday parties,” Robertson said in an interview. “It’s really towards the future of American competitiveness and energy security, which we believe is national security.”
The supply risks behind the designation are concentrated abroad. Qatar's helium exports have been severely curtailed by Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz as a result of its war with Israel and the U.S.
Iranian strikes on Qatar's infrastructure have also affected supply. Russia, one of the other top helium producers alongside the United States, imposed temporary export controls on helium in April to protect its domestic supply.
The United States is the world's largest producer of both natural gas and helium, and helium is primarily produced as a byproduct of natural gas processing. Even so, U.S. output is constrained.
The country produced 81 million cubic meters of helium in 2025, or 43% of the global supply, and exported 38 million cubic meters of that. Annual production has run at roughly 80 million cubic meters since 2021.
Large reserves sit in Wyoming, Kansas, Texas, Oklahoma, Colorado and Utah. But according to the department, helium extraction plants are at their limits, and it takes years to permit and build new ones, which continues to constrain U.S. production.
Federal data shows the plants extracting the most helium, as of 2023, were located in Kansas, Texas, Colorado, New Mexico, Arizona and Oklahoma. The constraints have a historical dimension.
The United States once kept a strategic national stockpile of helium in Texas, much like the Strategic Petroleum Reserve. Congress mandated in 2013 that it be privatized, and the Bureau of Land Management completed the sale of the federal helium system to the industrial gas company Messer in 2024.
Some in the helium industry had urged the government to make the designation formal. The North American gas exploration company Avanti Helium Corp. says it is urgent, and that an increase in North American supply is needed to avoid becoming dependent on foreign sources.
The U.S. Geological Survey included helium on a 2018 list of critical minerals, but later lists omitted it because the domestic supply of helium was considered secure. The United States designates both critical minerals and critical materials, and there is some crossover between the two lists.
Greeshma Gadikota, director of the Lenfast Center for Sustainable Energy at Columbia University, said that despite environmental concerns with recovering helium from natural gas, there are also opportunities.
“If we burn the natural gas, there are a lot of CO2 emissions associated with that,” Gadikota said. "But if you just extract the helium and use it, the uses of it don't contribute necessarily to greenhouse gas emissions.
“So from a climate standpoint, if we are going to continue down the line of extracting natural gas and recovering helium," she added, “I would prefer to see natural gas being used in a form where we directly produce hydrogen and we produce solid carbon.” Hydrogen is a clean burning fuel, and solid carbon can provide permanent carbon sequestration.
“We can effectively consolidate everything from raw materials to finished product in terms of manufacturing in the United States and rely less on overseas,” Gadikota said. "It brings more refining, recovery, use capabilities to the U.S. and actually justifies any investments of U.S. taxpayer dollars in initiatives related to helium production and refining."

articles.title_orig: King Apple is taking Wall Street’s top spot back from Nvidia — for the fifth time
articles.title_zh: King Apple is taking Wall Street’s top spot back from Nvidia — for the fifth time
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Apple ( AAPL ) is taking Wall Street's crown back from Nvidia — for the fifth time.
Apple briefly topped Nvidia in market value on Friday. It's a move Apple has made before, and it has rarely stuck.
Apple and Nvidia ( NVDA ) are each worth about $5.1 trillion, and the gap between them was less than 1% at Thursday's close. The flip came alongside a record run for Apple's stock and the day the tech giant's $1,999 iPhone Duo hit stores , capping a battle investors had been watching all morning. Nvidia has since moved back into the lead.
For most of the past decade, this wasn't much of a contest. Apple closed as the most valuable US-listed company in about 7 of every 10 sessions since October 2015. Microsoft ( MSFT ) took the top spot in stretches, Amazon ( AMZN ) held it for 12 sessions in early 2019, and Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ) got exactly one day in 2016.
Then the AI boom rewrote the leaderboard.
Nvidia first closed at No. 1 on June 18, 2024. It has held the spot almost without a break since June 2025, interrupted only by a four-session Apple run in late July.
Apple has reclaimed the crown from Nvidia four times before today. Only once did it last, when the DeepSeek scare sank chip stocks in January 2025 and Apple held on into the spring.
Since the start of 2024, the No. 1 spot has changed hands two dozen times, according to Yahoo Finance calculations.
This time, the two stocks are heading in opposite directions. Apple closed Thursday at a record. Nvidia sits about 11% below its Oct. 6 record close after this month's chip rout .
Since that Oct. 6 close, which was also the S&P 500's ( ^IXIC ) record, Apple is the only megacap stock in the green. It's up 4%.
Watch whether Apple can finish the day on top. It hasn't since July 30.
The next big test comes on Wednesday, when Microsoft and Alphabet report earnings. They rank third and fourth, each worth about $3.9 trillion.

articles.title_orig: Duchess of Sussex was told of ‘disturbing allegations’ against her father in 2018
articles.title_zh: Duchess of Sussex was told of ‘disturbing allegations’ against her father in 2018
articles.content_orig:
Meghan reveals she was made aware of ‘disturbing allegations’ against him in 2018 by Met police
The Duchess of Sussex has said she is “deeply distressed” over accusations involving child sexual abuse images against her estranged father, Thomas Markle Sr, and revealed she was made aware of “disturbing allegations” against him in 2018 by the Metropolitan police.
Meghan issued a statement after the Sun newspaper published claims that her half-brother Thomas Markle Jr alleged he had found a stash of images belonging to their father at his former home in the Philippines.
In an interview with the Daily Mail, Markle Sr denied possessing child sexual abuse images, calling the accusations “sick lies”.
It is understood that authorities in the UK previously told Meghan that allegations made about her father in a 2018 letter sent to Scotland Yard, and subsequently shared with her by the police, were being investigated.
Meghan was informed by the Met of the allegations in the summer shortly after her wedding, it is believed.
In a statement through her spokesperson, Meghan said: “I am deeply distressed at the news that has come to light in the last 24 hours, and my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed.
“In 2018, a letter was sent to the Metropolitan police and Royalty and Specialist Protection [Rasp]. That letter was subsequently shared with me. It made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father and I was given assurances that these were being investigated.
“I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications’ distortion over the years, any distance from my father, and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children, was for one reason: to protect them. I trusted that the authorities were doing the same for other families.
“Although the breadth of what has now been uncovered is more sickening than one could ever imagine, my sincerest hope is that justice will be fully served and that the priority remains the safety and protection of innocent children.”
The 2018 letter was understood to have been shared with Meghan by the Rasp unit within the Met police.
It is understood the Met has not previously investigated Markle Snr, nor is it currently doing so. The force said it was making internal inquiries regarding officers from Rasp being involved in the passing on of a letter.
A Met spokesperson said: “We are aware of media reports that officers from the Met’s royalty and specialist protection command were involved in the passing on of a letter in 2018. We are undertaking inquiries internally in an effort to confirm this.”
Markle Sr has been estranged from the duchess since he failed to attend her wedding to Prince Harry on health grounds, and he has never met his grandchildren Prince Archie, seven, and Princess Lilibet, five.
The Sun reported that Markle Jr told detectives in the Philippines he had discovered “hundreds, if not thousands” of child sexual abuse images on computers and mobile phones stored in four large boxes at the home in Cebu where Markle Sr was living until he returned to the US in May after having a stroke.
Markle Jr, 60, said he had also contacted the FBI in the US, the Sun reported.
The undersecretary for the Philippines’ justice department, Nicholas Ty, told the BBC the matter was being investigated by a human trafficking and child sexual exploitation taskforce in Cebu.
The interior secretary, Jonvic Remulla, separately told the BBC that national police had secured Markle Sr’s computer to conduct a comprehensive digital forensic examination. Remulla said it would take “one week to get the forensic [results]”.
Meghan’s father has denied possessing child sexual abuse images, telling the Daily Mail that the accusations were “sick lies”.
He told the newspaper that the computers had not been in his possession since he left Rosarito, Mexico, with his son in January 2025 and moved to the Philippines “for a fresh start”.
Speaking from a rehabilitation centre in Florida, where he is learning to walk with a prosthetic limb after his left leg was amputated because of a blood clot, he told the Mail: “I’m shocked, I’m hurt and I’m very upset that my son is making these accusations against me. I could never do what I’m being accused of. It’s the worst thing anyone could accuse me of.
“This is bullshit. It’s just a bunch of lies. It’s sick. I have no idea why Tom is trying to destroy me with these lies.”
Meghan’s half-sister Samantha Markle has defended their father, accusing her brother Markle Jr of “making up lies” to make money.
She told the Mail: “There is no merit in these disgusting allegations whatsoever and my brother is disgusting for making them up. He wants to destroy our dad. Shame on him.”
She alleged her brother made the allegations days after their father cut off his funds, “and once the money stopped he made up the most outrageous lies he could to make money from the media”.
She alleged the computers were not in her father’s possession for two years and he could have been set up. “That leaves a lot of room for tampering,” she said.

articles.title_zh: Designers’ notes: The River of Bones rules
articles.content_orig:
Designers’ notes: The River of Bones rules
Arcane Journal – The River of Bones is packed with new background and rules. Having learnt about the lore earlier in the week, we sat down with the Warhammer: The Old World studio to discover more about the rules.
JTY: There’s a wealth of new content in this Arcane Journal, both for Tomb Kings of Khemri and Wood Elf Realms players, as well as magic items and battlefield rules for everyone. But you won’t need this supplement in order to use the new Tomb Kings models – the profiles for all of those can be found in Ravening Hordes .*
Dave: Arcane Journal – The River of Bones contains two new scenarios. The first is a multi-player Battle March scenario for four players, and the second recreates the battle on the banks of the Crystal Mere, the mysterious lake in the heart of Athel Loren where the Tomb Kings and Wood Elves clashed. Alongside these is a really fun table of rules for Enchanted Terrain , the type of thing a traveller might encounter in the depths of Athel Loren. This can be good or bad depending on what you roll. A low roll might see a unit covered in Clawing Mud suffer modifiers to its Movement, or fall subject to Stupidity due to a Fungal Enchantment . But a high roll can result in a unit gaining Regeneration after discovering the Waters of Rejuvenation , or getting a Ward save after securing the Blessings of the Ancient Wood .
JTY: In the Champions of Nehekhara section you’ll find new rules for using the Tomb Kings of Khemri in games of Battle March. For example, the Arch Hierophant enables players to field a Battle March army without having to have a Hierophant on the battlefield. Instead, the army is empowered by the machinations of a more distant Liche Priest. This gives more freedom when writing your muster list because you aren’t obliged to include two characters, whilst still allowing you to resurrect slain models as normal. Although, of course, this is not without risk…
Dave: Speaking of muster lists, Arcane Journal – The River of Bones contains two new Armies of Infamy. The first focuses on the Tomb Kings themselves, in particular the Barrow Kingdoms. These are the long forgotten vassal states of ancient Nehekhara, the fringes of a vast empire conquered in Settra’s lifetime, where occupying armies merged with those of barbarian warlords keen to emulate the practices of Nehekhara in everything from religion and burial rites to organising an army.
Where this army differs from the norm is in the options. Liche Priests gain access to the Lores of Battle Magic and Dark Magic , the better to represent the sorts of shaman common in these ancient realms, whilst both Skeleton Horsemen and Skeleton Chariots** can be upgraded, making them the ideal hard-hitting bodyguard to accompany a long dead scion of the Great Land.
JTY: But that’s not all, there’s also an Army of Infamy for the Wood Elf Realms, the Spirits of the Forest. This army focuses on the more magical elements of Athel Loren, encouraging armies that contain lots of Dryads, Treekin and Treemen. In terms of special rules, the list gives players access to Blessings of the Elder Wood , a number of magical upgrades for their Treemen and Branchwraiths , effectively giving them access to their own unique magic items.
This is followed by rules for Wood Elf Kindreds, the various clans associated with different parts of the great forest. These reflect how Kinbands, or units, from different Kindreds fight. The Kinbands of Cavaroc , for example, gain Vanguard, whilst the Kinbands of Torgovann get to choose a non-magical combat weapon and improve its AP.
The Kinbands of Cavaroc (+15 points per unit)
Kinbands that hail from the open plains of Cavaroc are swift of foot, capable of covering vast distances in a single march.
A unit belonging to this Kindred gains the Vanguard special rule and improves the Movement characteristic of the unit and their mounts (should they have one) by 1.
The Kinbands Of Torgovann (+1 points per model)
Sharing their realm with the Forge of Starlight, the Kindreds of Torgovann are armed with the finest weapons to be found in Athel Loren.
Choose one non-magical combat weapon wielded by this unit and improve the Armour Piercing characteristic of that weapon by 1. The chosen weapon must be clearly noted on your muster list.
Dave: Finally, there is a brand new set of common magic items, this time themed around the sort of ancient artefact that might be found in the depths of a long-forgotten barrow mound somewhere in the foothills of the Vaults of the Grey Mountains.
As usual, this section includes magic weapons, armour, talismans and banners, as well as enchanted and arcane items, all of which are very useful, but many of which bear an unfortunate curse!*** Take the Armour of Dust , for example; this suit of full plate armour reduces the wearer’s Toughness if they roll a 1 when making an armour save. Or there’s the vial of Barrow Dirt , a single-use item which the bearer can throw at the enemy like a Breath Weapon, with Strength 3, an AP of -3 and Multiple Wounds (2). However, if they fail an Initiative test after doing so, they risk being hit as well.
Vials of dust scraped from the floor of ancient tombs can desiccate the flesh and sap the strength of those they come into contact with.
0-1 per model. Single use. Barrow-dirt is a breath weapon with the following profile:
Breath Weapon, Magical Attacks, Multiple Wounds (2)
Notes: After using Barrow-dirt, the bearer must make an Initiative test. If this test is failed, they risk being hit as if they were partially under the flame template.
Thanks, folks! The new Arcane Journal is available for pre-order tomorrow, along with the Host of Nehekhara Army Reinforcement Set. There’s never been a better time to start an implacable undead army or to grow your existing legions.
* But don’t forget to keep your eyes on the latest FAQ and Errata . ** The new Skeleton Chariots are on a different base size compared to the old kits – download the PDF errata now. *** That’s on you for taking mysterious magic items from forgotten barrow mounds.

articles.title_orig: In Troubled Times, Finland’s Public Broadcaster Has an Answer: Puppies
articles.title_zh: In Troubled Times, Finland’s Public Broadcaster Has an Answer: Puppies
articles.content_orig:
Show features live chat sessions with breeders, a podcast and updates on dogs’ progress from birth to weigh-ins
A 24-hour Finnish TV show dedicated entirely to the live progress of a dog and her six newborn puppies is drawing millions of viewers.
As well as a 24-hour webcam, Pentulive (Puppy Live) includes live evening chat sessions with the dogs’ breeder, a podcast and an instant notification service that updates followers on the puppies’ progress – from their birth to weigh-ins and first nail trims – for eight weeks.
This is the sixth season of the hit show by the broadcaster Yle, and the latest contribution to the growing Nordic cultural phenomenon of “slow TV”.
The trend started in Norway in 2009 with Bergensbanen, a seven-hour train journey broadcast on NRK , and was followed in Sweden by SVT’s Den stora älgvandringen (The Great Moose Migration), which features unnarrated glimpses of moose from the north of the country making their annual journey to summer grazing grounds.
Pentulive has long attracted interest from outside Finland, but this year it is also being broadcast in Sweden (under the name Valparna live ). Yle recently announced that it had also sold the format to a broadcaster in the Netherlands.
Ville Alijoki, the editorial manager of Yle’s factual journalism, said: “There’s a certain magic to it, something that people miss when this world is sometimes quite dark.”
On Saturday, the lagotto romagnolo puppies – four male and two female – will mark their two-week birthday by being officially named after a vote by viewers. Among the nominations are Martha, Timo, Ronja and Dante.
In mid-December, the puppies will leave their mother, Hilkka, and be adopted by new families.
Yle said the current season of Pentulive was on a path to break previous viewing records. Across its first two weeks, the stream has been watched for more than 1m hours, and the show has attracted 1.85 million unique viewers across all related content.
Fans say the puppies offer a relaxing break from work, and comfort from stress, loneliness and illness.
after newsletter promotion
Pirjo Koskinen, a science journalist who came up with the Pentulive concept with the aim of educating viewers on the latest dog research and the importance of the first few weeks of a dog’s life, said the show provided “relief from the terrible things happening in the world”.
She said: “Wars, bombing, climate change, habitat loss etc make us anxious and you can escape, for at least a moment, by watching the canine family.”
Watching the mother and breeder take care of the puppies was like watching “a loop of love and caring”, she said.
“It’s real and we are in the basics of life: the miracle of birth, growth and development. It’s so heartwarming to see eyes opening and first clumsy steps, and it’s happening right now. That brings us joy, but also many funny moments during eight weeks.”

articles.title_orig: Meghan ‘deeply distressed’ by report alleging her dad possessed child sexual abuse images
articles.title_zh: Meghan ‘deeply distressed’ by report alleging her dad possessed child sexual abuse images
articles.content_orig:
BREAKING: Trump administration sues to block Alaska Senate certification if Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan loses in November
LONDON — Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex , said Friday that she was “deeply distressed” by a report alleging that her estranged father, Thomas Markle Sr. , possessed child sexual abuse images, adding that she was informed by police of “disturbing allegations” against him in 2018.
In a statement Friday, Meghan addressed the report that her father was being investigated over claims he kept child sexual abuse videos and images at his home in the Philippines. “The breadth of what has now been uncovered is more sickening than one could ever imagine,” said Meghan, who has in recent years had a limited and fraught relationship with her father. He did not attend her wedding to Prince Harry in 2018, drawing widespread media scrutiny.
The allegations against Markle Sr. were first reported Thursday by The Sun newspaper, a British tabloid, which reported that his son had informed police after he said he found “hundreds, if not thousands” of child sex abuse images in boxes at his father’s home. The Sun published a photo it said showed his son, Thomas  Markle Jr., signing a sworn statement it said he had submitted to police and quoted him as saying: “I won’t speak to my father ever again unless I’m called to give evidence against him.”
Markle Sr., 82, denied the reported allegations, calling them “sick lies” in a statement to Britain’s Daily Mail newspaper. He added they were “the worst thing anyone could accuse me of.”
NBC News was not immediately able to identify a contact for  Markle Sr., who the Daily Mail reported was now in a Florida rehab center recovering from surgery.
Markle Jr. told the Sun that he had reported his discovery to the FBI, as well as local Philippine authorities. NBC News has reached out to the FBI for comment, which did not immediately respond.
The Philippines’ justice department confirmed Friday that “the matter is under investigation” but otherwise declined to “provide further details at this time.”
Police in Cebu City, the location of Markle Sr.’s home in the Philippines, and London’s Metropolitan Police did not immediately respond to requests for comment from NBC News.
In the rare statement Friday, Meghan said that she had chosen to keep her children, Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, away from her father “for one reason: to protect them.”
“I am deeply distressed at the news that has come to light in the last 24 hours, and my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed,” she said in the statement.
Meghan said that she had been made aware of a letter sent to the British police and other authorities in 2018, that “made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father and I was given assurances that these were being investigated.”
“I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications’ distortion over the years, any distance from my father and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children, was for one reason: to protect them,” she added.
“Although the breadth of what has now been uncovered is more sickening than one could ever imagine, my sincerest hope is that justice will be fully served and that the priority remains the safety and protection of innocent children,” Meghan said.
Asked by NBC News when Meghan was made aware of the letter to the Metropolitan Police, a spokesman for the couple said it was in the summer of 2018, after her wedding with Harry.
Separately, a source close to the couple told NBC News that Meghan’s decision not to speak publicly eight years ago should be understood in a particular context: “When she was made aware of these allegations in 2018 after they were reported to the police, they remained just that — allegations.”
“To have repeated them publicly at that stage would not only have potentially exposed her to civil action for making unsubstantiated claims, but she had also been advised that doing so could jeopardize any subsequent investigation,” the source added.
Markle Sr. told the Daily Mail he had not spoken to his son “for months” and said “these terrible lies are being made against me with no proof.” He added that he would “welcome an investigation” into the matter and labeled the accusations “a bunch of lies.”
His daughter, Samantha Markle, also told the Daily Mail of her brother’s allegations: “there is no merit in these disgusting allegations whatsoever ... He wants to destroy our dad. Shame on him.”
NBC News did not immediately receive responses to requests for comment from Markle Jr. or Samantha Markle — Meghan’s half-siblings.
Markle Sr. married Meghan’s mother, Doria Ragland, in 1979 and they subsequently divorced in 1987.
Meghan, 45, and Harry, 42, moved back to the United Kingdom earlier this summer after several years in the United States.
The couple made their first joint public appearance last week visiting charities in central England. King Charles III has made clear that their return does not signal a return to active royal life. Harry, however, has said recently that he wants his disagreements with his family to “work out.”
Adela Suliman is a breaking-news editor and reporter for NBC News in London.

(Kitco NewsWire) - Spot gold and silver prices were sharply lower in late U.S. trading Thursday, as renewed Middle East tensions sent crude oil prices higher, reinforcing inflation concerns and expectations for additional Federal Reserve tightening. A sharp selloff in technology shares and falling Treasury yields failed to generate sustained safe-haven demand for bullion, while silver faced additional pressure from concerns about industrial demand and slowing economic activity. At the time of the latest verified late-afternoon reading, spot gold was trading near $4,021.20 an ounce, down $119.10, or 2.88%, while spot silver was trading near $54.440, down $3.410, or 5.90%.
Market positioning remains divided between persistent inflation pressure, weaker economic activity and growing financial-market instability. September consumer inflation increased 0.6% on the month and 3.7% annually , while producer prices rose 1.3% and 6.3%, respectively . Fed funds futures continue to favor no change at the Oct. 27-28 Federal Reserve meeting, with recent pricing indicating approximately an 84% probability of a pause and a 16% probability of a 25-basis-point increase. December tightening remains the central market expectation, although the precise probabilities have fluctuated as traders reassess growth risks and the inflationary impact of elevated energy prices. Treasury yields declined Thursday as selling in technology shares encouraged demand for government bonds. However, falling yields failed to support gold, suggesting that precious metals positioning, liquidation pressure and the outlook for further monetary tightening remained dominant considerations.
The Federal Reserve remains in its premeeting communications blackout, shifting attention to Friday's preliminary October manufacturing and services purchasing managers' indexes at 9:45 a.m. EDT and the final University of Michigan consumer sentiment survey at 10 a.m. EDT. The reports will provide further evidence on business activity, consumer confidence and inflation expectations before next week's monetary policy decision.
The Fed's Oct. 27-28 meeting and the subsequent release of September personal consumption expenditures inflation data on Oct. 29 will provide more substantial tests of market expectations for December tightening. Softer activity readings and easing inflation expectations could reduce pressure on yields and improve gold's outlook, while stronger economic data and persistent price pressures would reinforce the prospect of additional interest rate increases.
The Strait of Hormuz and U.S.-Iran situation remained a significant source of financial-market uncertainty Thursday as renewed attacks on commercial shipping and energy infrastructure increased concerns about regional escalation. Reports of damaged vessels and threats to maritime traffic were accompanied by renewed security concerns involving Saudi Arabian energy facilities, while Washington and Tehran remained divided over the conditions for reopening normal commercial shipping through the strait. Diplomatic contacts have not produced a confirmed settlement, and uncertainty about possible additional military action has complicated efforts to stabilize the corridor. Although alternative pipelines, rerouting and ship-to-ship transfers have helped restore aggregate Middle Eastern oil exports, direct tanker movements through Hormuz remain substantially disrupted. The continuing security threat has sustained an elevated geopolitical risk premium in crude oil prices despite the partial recovery in regional exports.
For gold, the escalation presents competing influences. The prospect of further military confrontation supports defensive demand, but rising crude oil prices threaten to prolong inflation and increase pressure on the Fed to maintain restrictive monetary policy. Thursday's decline in gold despite lower Treasury yields highlights the limited effectiveness of traditional safe-haven support during the latest liquidation. Silver underperformed as the broader precious metals selloff coincided with weakening equity markets and concerns about industrial demand. The combination of high energy costs, slowing interest rate-sensitive activity and persistent inflation risks continues to complicate the outlook for both metals.
North American equity markets finished mixed to sharply lower Thursday as renewed selling in artificial intelligence-related shares overwhelmed gains in other sectors. The Dow Jones Industrial Average edged up 11.89 points, or less than 0.1%, to close at 52,867.98, while the S&P 500 lost 93.74 points, or 1.21%, to 7,663.43, its largest daily decline since July. The Nasdaq Composite tumbled 694.00 points, or 2.60%, to 26,008.86, pressured by renewed concerns about the financing and profitability of artificial intelligence investment. The Russell 2000 gained 3.01 points, or approximately 0.11%, to 2,784.03. The contrast between heavy technology-sector losses and gains across a majority of individual stocks indicated that selling remained concentrated in highly valued growth shares rather than extending uniformly across the U.S. equity market.
European equity markets closed lower Thursday, pressured by rising crude oil prices, weaker corporate earnings sentiment and concerns about government finances. The pan-European Stoxx 600 declined approximately 1.05%, while Germany's DAX lost around 1.1%. France's CAC 40 fell approximately 1.4%, reflecting continuing fiscal uncertainty and pressure on French financial assets. The U.K.'s FTSE 100 declined approximately 0.3%, outperforming continental benchmarks, while Italy's FTSE MIB dropped roughly 2.5% and Spain's IBEX 35 lost approximately 2.1%. Banks, miners and other economically sensitive shares were among the weakest sectors as investors assessed the implications of higher energy prices and elevated borrowing costs for European economic growth.
The key outside markets see crude oil prices higher as renewed attacks and military threats involving Iran increase concerns about Middle Eastern energy exports. Brent crude traded above $113.00 a barrel during the U.S. session, while WTI approached $100.00. The yield on the benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury note declined as demand for government bonds strengthened during the equity selloff.
