articles.title_orig: Louvre and other museums closing for Saturday protests as French authorities deploy 70,000 officers
articles.title_zh: Louvre and other museums closing for Saturday protests as French authorities deploy 70,000 officers
articles.content_orig:
Guardian Europe columnists Rokhaya Diallo and Alexander Hurst answered your questions about the recent protests in France, the role of the French police, foreign influence and the upcoming presidential election.
After weeks of protests and a weekend of riots in which a town hall was set ablaze, 2,000-plus shops were looted, 2,300 people were arrested and 1,000 police injured, the repercussions for France – for its society and its economy – continue. Allegations of police brutality surfaced, and the violent protests unnerved investors, resulting in a debt sell-off , with borrowing costs rising higher than for Greece. All of this ahead of a hotly contested presidential election that’s now just six months away.
The French government’s escalating financial problems were covered by the Guardian’s Europe correspondent Jon Henley who wrote: “France’s national debt, at 119% of GDP, is at its highest level since 1946 . Its budget deficit, at 5.1%, is also among the highest in the EU. There is just no money in the bank to ease the cost of living squeeze that brought 550,000 people on to the streets on Saturday.”
Columnist Paul Taylor commented that “Last weekend’s violence has increased the likelihood of a law-and-order backlash among voters that could propel (Marine) Le Pen into the Élysée Palace. But if the financial situation worsens and the campaign turns on who can save the economy, she may yet lose out to a candidate who is firm on security and more orthodox on fiscal policy.”
And the Guardian’s editorial noted that “In an increasingly febrile atmosphere, France is heading towards a seismic reckoning in May. Alarmingly, the civil strife witnessed at the weekend may only be a foretaste of what is to come.”
What are your views on the riots, their causes and their aftermath? Are they paving a path to the presidency for Le Pen? In his final months in charge, can embattled incumbent Emmanuel Macron meaningfully address the situation in which France finds herself?
France-based Guardian Europe columnists Rokhaya Diallo and Alexander Hurst will be live here at 1500BST today to answer your questions on what happened, why, and where France goes from here.
Post your questions in the comments below or email conversations@theguardian.com
Thank you so much for all of these questions! France is always a fascinating place to observe and interact with and write about – I hope it stays more fascinating than worrying as the election progresses on.
Yasmin Maassarani asks: My question to both speakers is, I see one of main issues is that grievances in movements such as these are usually not addressed. This, in turn, leads to apathy and more disengagement in the wider political system. How can this youth movement maintain momentum through constructive dialogue and concrete change?
double quotation mark Rokhaya: Indeed, Macron’s presidency has accumulated frustrations by failing to respond adequately to successive demands for change. Let’s take the example of the Citizens’ Convention on Climate launched by Macron in 2019: people who took part were so disappointed with the government’s eventual response to their proposals they rated it just 3.3 out of 10.
The controversial pension reform was pushed through despite sustained opposition, and millions of people taking to the streets, while the 2024 legislative elections left many voters feeling that their rejection of Macron’s policies had been disregarded. The latest protest movement also draws strength from those accumulated disappointments.
The young people mobilising have much to gain by keeping their demands clear, maintaining the inventiveness they have already shown. They can also build alliances with other movements while preserving their own voice. They have been documenting instances of police brutality and challenging accusations about their autonomy i.e. the suggestion that they were being manipulated by political actors. To push back in that way is efficient: their grievances must remain central to the debate.
To turn momentum into concrete change, they can demand public commitments, deadlines and a transparent account of what has actually been delivered. Regular assemblies and accountable representatives can help keep participants involved and prevent negotiations from becoming detached from the movement.
But responsibility for constructive dialogue also lies with the government. Young people cannot be expected to sustain faith in democratic participation indefinitely if the response they run up against systematically is repression.
double quotation mark Alexander: I think the high schoolers timed their protest quite well to set some of the terms of the election and get on everyone’s political agenda. One of the toughest things is breaking through and getting attention. They’ve done that, and now they need to make sure that the debate doesn’t get derailed into this new law and order debate that Saturday’s chaos produced.
It’s also important not to only try to go top-down by focusing exclusively on the presidential race. Of course that’s important, but political power is also built ground up and locally, which can then support the low-hum of actual policy work once the media cycle inevitably moves on to the next thing.
Alix Davis asks: Regarding the original demonstrations by students protesting against the lack of replacement teachers and the run-down state of their school buildings, has there been any government acknowledgment of those complaints as justified?
double quotation mark Rokhaya: Yes, the government has acknowledged that some of the students’ demands are legitimate and it has announced measures to address teacher shortages but it took weeks of mobilisation, serious injuries to young people and growing international concern for their grievances to receive this level of political attention.
I also find the decision to launch a platform asking students to describe their problems insulting. They had already explained them, repeatedly: teachers not replaced, overcrowded classrooms and buildings unfit for learning. I detailed some of the conditions facing pupils in French schools in a Guardian article in 2023, Parents and teachers had raised their concerns through official channels long before this mobilisation.
Presenting this now as a listening exercise as if the government lacked information is inadequate. Asking young people to submit their experiences again, while their peers are being injured in demonstrations seems like another way of postponing action.
double quotation mark Alexander: Superficially, yes, because they more or less have to. But concretely, no. Macron gave a speech that satisfied exactly zero people in which he basically said (and I’m paraphrasing here) “I’m out in six months, good luck”, and then flew off to Saudi Arabia, which should tell you a lot.
One of Macron’s major flaws has been extending promises that people could express discontent in other ways and be listened to, only to show through his dismissal of those mechanisms (the “cahiers de doléance”, the “grand national debate”, the Citizens Convention on Climate), that it was a false promise, and that he wasn’t actually going to take them seriously.
He wildly overestimated his election as evidence of broad support for his platform, rather than as a cordon sanitaire against Le Pen, and he tried to govern in a top down way, rather than understanding that he didn’t have that political capital and that his entire approach to governing needed to be revisited.

articles.title_orig: Engineers perform delicate operation on explosives-packed World War II shipwreck, but bombs remain in place
articles.title_zh: Engineers perform delicate operation on explosives-packed World War II shipwreck, but bombs remain in place
articles.content_orig:
Sheerness, England — A delicate operation aimed at preventing an 82-year-old U.S. shipwreck packed with tons of World War II explosives from unleashing a potentially catastrophic tidal wave on London has been completed. But while the most imminent danger has been addressed, the explosives remain inside the rusting wreck of the SS Richard Montgomery on the riverbed, and experts aren't taking their eyes off it.
The Montgomery, one of about 2,700 Liberty ships built in the U.S. to support the Allied war effort, was grounded on a sandbar off the town of Sheerness in the Thames Estuary, just 40 miles from the British capital, in August 1944. It was carrying munitions intended to support the Allies following the D-Day landings.
The vessel broke apart during salvage efforts and sank, with an estimated 1,500 tons of explosives in its cargo holds.
The ship's three rusting masts protruding from the water had been a familiar sight to residents and passing vessels for decades. But recent surveys revealed increasing deterioration in the structure, raising fears the masts could collapse and trigger an explosion.
"The vessel was starting to lean and deteriorate, so they could see some of the structures around the mast starting to collapse," Nolan Conway, a naval architect with Florida-based marine salvage firm Resolve Marine Group, which was contracted to remove the masts, told CBS News.
"The fear is the masts could have fallen onto the cargo itself, causing it to detonate," he said. "Some of the munitions are believed to be fused munitions with pressure fuses, so something like an impact could potentially set them off."
U.K. maritime minister Keir Mather told lawmakers in the House of Commons this week that the "complex project requiring specialist program, engineering and risk management expertise" had been completed ahead of schedule and on budget, with all three of the masts removed at a cost of just under $13 million, according to The Guardian .
Mather said in the U.K. Parliament that the masts had put "significant load on the structure and their removal has reduced that risk and supports the long-term safe management of the site."
The government has long maintained an exclusion zone around the wreck, which is about 1.5 miles off the Sheerness coast.
Mather told lawmakers the wreck would "continue to be subject to continuous monitoring and control via the established exclusion zone."
Removing the remaining explosives would carry considerable risks, and the consequences of an explosion remain the subject of debate among experts.
"The impact of this wreck detonating is unpredictable," Conway said. "Estimates range from impacting the shoreline, to creating a tidal wave that could travel up the Thames, to a rather minor event that could potentially just close a nearby shipping channel. There's a large range of impacts, but none of them are really good."
Officials continue to assess the overall risk of an explosion as low, but the deteriorating condition of the masts prompted authorities to act.
Conway said the challenge for the firm was to devise a way to remove the masts without disturbing the sunken ship's hull and the perilous cargo inside, or putting the people doing the work at risk.
"How can you cut off that mast without vibrating or impacting the wreck?" he said. "We designed a custom lifting frame to safely pick it up without the mast swinging or swaying as we lifted it free of the wreck."
Engineers used a remotely operated underwater diamond-wire saw that clamps "around the mast with hydraulic arms and passes the saw through without getting divers in the water," Conway explained.
The removal of the masts marks the end of a distinctive chapter in the wreck's history. The masts, visible above the estuary since World War II, are expected to be preserved for public display.
Mather, the U.K. maritime minister, said the masts had been moved to a local museum, the Historic Dockyard Chatham, and would be displayed "in recognition of the historic significance of the SS Richard Montgomery and its role in supporting the Allied forces' efforts during World War II."
More than eight decades after the ship failed to reach the battlefields of Europe, the Montgomery and its dangerous cargo will remain where it came to rest, now entirely hidden from view, but far from forgotten.

articles.title_orig: New for Necromunda in 2027
articles.title_zh: New for Necromunda in 2027
articles.content_orig:
New for Necromunda in 2027
There’s an exciting year ahead for fans of Necromunda, with a lineup more stuffed than the questionably-sourced contents of a back-alley Scabber’s overcoat. There will be new miniatures, new terrain, new vehicles and new expansions. However, there won’t be a Roleplay expansion.
After careful consideration we’ve decided to focus our efforts on providing even more great minis for the core game.
Don’t worry – all the minis we showcased in the Big Autumn Preview are still on their way, and will be available for use in standard games of Necromunda.
Looking ahead to 2027, the new releases will cover multiple key gangs and locations, so here's a roadmap, because everybody loves roadmaps.*
Starting in the spring, we go back to the ash wastes with new rules expansions and the biggest plastic vehicle kit yet released for Necromunda.
Then, those brave enough can once more enter the cursed depths of the Underhells in search of ancient archeotech, where among other things they will bump into new Fighters for the Malstrain Genestealer cults.
And then we return to the still-smoking urban sprawl of Cinderak City, one of the conflict flashpoints of the recent Aranthian Succession . This is accompanied by support for some of the original underhive crews of Necromunda, including hulking new brutes.
And we’re still not done for 2027. Rounding out the year, there will be new mercenaries and gunslingers, set on hunting down their unfortunate bounties in whatever dank or irradiated corner of Necromunda they sought to hide.
Alongside all of the above, you’ll also get support for other gangs, scenery, and regular rules expansions.
And still set to arrive this year is a major expansion for the House of Iron in the shape of three flexible new multipart plastic kits, offering an enormous range of new cosmetic and wargear options for your Orlock gang.
We’ll cover them all in more detail soon, so check back regularly, and sign up to the Warhammer newsletter to stay up to date with the latest Necromunda news.
* Everybody except the Ash Waste Nomads, but they just hate roads!

articles.title_orig: Weil Gotshal Loses More Top Lawyers as Merger Talks Collapse
articles.title_zh: Weil Gotshal Loses More Top Lawyers as Merger Talks Collapse
articles.content_orig:
Weil Gotshal & Manges and Willkie Farr & Gallagher have ended discussions over a possible merger, intensifying pressure on Weilâs leaders as many of its top partners take jobs elsewhere.
The talks were ended last night after the two sides had signed a non-disclosure agreement to discuss a tieup, two people familiar with the matter said. Willkie was the law firm Bloomberg Law reported Weil was in discussions with earlier this week.
On Thursday, at least some top partners at Weil had been holding discussions with their colleagues to build excitement for the possible tie-up, according to a person familiar with those discussions. By the end of the day, the merger talks were off.
The development came as more Weil partners headed for the exits.
The co-managing partner of Weilâs corporate department, Lyuba Goltser, plans to join Sidley Austin, according to a person familiar with the move. Davis Polk & Wardwell plans to bring on appellate litigator Drew Tulumello, another person said. And the Wall Street Journal reported Paul Weiss is hiring securities litigation partner Caroline Zalka. Tulumello and Zalka are members of Weilâs management committee.
It is unclear if Weil has lined up merger discussions with other firms, or whether its leaders will seek to do so. But continued departures of top partners risks setting off a so-called talent run, where partners begin to leave not because they can do better financially at another firm, but because they fear being left behind at a depleted firm.
âLateral movement for âI can do betterâ is very common,â said David McGowan, a law professor at the University of San Diego. âAnd the run on the bank metaphor happens when âI can do betterâ reaches a scale at which it turns into âI donât want to be left holding the bag.ââ
Some previous law firm mergers have come together after discussions broke down with early suitors.
Shearman & Sterling broke off talks with Hogan Lovells in 2023 before tying up with Allen & Overy. Kaye Scholer and Arnold & Porter in 2016 reportedly ended discussions, only for the talks to revive and the firms to merge.
Spokespeople for Weil and Willkie did not respond to requests for comment.
Large law firms in the US and UK have been actively exploring mergers in a race to scale and hot market for high-end corporate partners. A Weil combination with Willkie would have created a massive firm with more than $4 billion in annual revenue, placing it among the five largest based in the US.
Weil has been rocked by a string of partner departures in recent weeks, with more expected to be formally announced. The departures include Michael Aiello, the powerful corporate department leader who in September announced he would leave for Cravath, Swaine & Moore.

articles.title_orig: Micron Stock Leads Chip Rebound. Dip Buyers Must Buckle Up as AI Chaos Swirls.
articles.title_zh: Micron Stock Leads Chip Rebound. Dip Buyers Must Buckle Up as AI Chaos Swirls.
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Some companies don't keep their ambitions secret. They swagger onto the stock market and draw plenty of attention with a splashy IPO and big promises (lookin' at you, Tesla ).
But some incredibly successful stocks are sleeper hits: They quietly sit on the market doing nothing until one day, bam! Their shares take off like a rocket, and everybody wonders how they didn't see it coming.
Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »
That's what happened to memory chipmaker Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU) in late 2025: Its shares had languished for years until a global memory shortage and AI data center boom took the stock stratospheric. Between June 25, 2025, and June 25, 2026, the chipmaker's shares grew more than 850%.
If you were lucky enough to invest $10,000 in Micron on that day in 2025, you'd have had $95,370 a year later. Even today, after shares have dropped 25% from those highs, you'd still have $70,970. Not enough, perhaps, to fund a full retirement, but a nice chunk of change.
So, what about right now? Could buying $10,000 in Micron today set you up for life?
It's ironic that even though Micron's share price has grown astronomically since June 2025, its price-to-earnings ratio -- how its share price compares to its profits -- has actually gone down. In June 2025, shares were trading at about 22 times earnings. In June 2026, at its peak, it traded at about 27 times earnings. Today, it's trading at about 12 times earnings.
Why would a wildly successful company that's grown its revenue by 256% and its per-share earnings by 879% in 16 months have a cheaper valuation than it did before?
The simple answer is that the market doesn't expect the good times to last, for two reasons.
The first reason is that this has happened before to memory chip stocks, and it didn't end well. Prices for dynamic RAM (DRAM) memory spiked in 2020-2021 during the pandemic tech-buying surge. After expanding capacity to meet that demand, memory producers wound up with a supply glut, and prices crashed in 2023.
This time around, Micron has tried to protect itself against such a price crash by signing multiyear supply deals with its customers to lock in price floors, allowing it to safely expand its capacity. That's a smart move, but the market is also concerned about competition.
Until now, three companies have had the global market for DRAM and high bandwidth memory (HBM) to themselves: Micron and South Korean companies Samsung Electronics (OTC: SSNLF) and SK Hynix (NASDAQ: SKHY). But all three are planning to expand capacity, while concerns about rapid expansion by Chinese manufacturers abound.
While it's possible that Micron's long-term contracts will allow it to continue to grow revenue and profits, a nervous market is unlikely to give it full credit for its success. It certainly seems doubtful that it will reach a $10 trillion valuation anytime soon (which would turn a $10,000 investment into $100,000).
Even if a $10,000 investment in Micron probably won't set you up for life, the ongoing growth of AI infrastructure deployment should make Micron a solid investment for years to come.

articles.title_orig: Romania blames Russia for drone that sinks cargo ship; 1 killed, 3 missing
articles.title_zh: Romania blames Russia for drone that sinks cargo ship; 1 killed, 3 missing
articles.content_orig:
A drone attack has hit and sunk a cargo vessel in the Black Sea, killing one crew member and leaving three missing
BUCHAREST, Romania -- A drone hit and sank a cargo vessel in the Black Sea on Friday, killing one crew member and leaving three missing, officials said, in the latest attack on commercial shipping in the region that has raised fears of an escalation in Russia's war against Ukraine.
Romanian naval authorities said that a search and rescue mission was underway after the ship caught fire and sank about 13 nautical miles (15 miles) east of the port city of Constanta, near Romania's territorial waters. The crew consisted of 10 Ukrainian citizens and three Azerbaijanis. Nine were rescued.
“This attack is a new example of the tragic consequences of Russia’s aggression against Ukraine,” Romanian President Nicusor Dan said. “It is time for Russia to take peace initiatives of the United States and Europe seriously, accept the ceasefire proposals and end the war.”
At least seven other cargo vessels have been attacked this month off the Black Sea coasts of NATO members Romania and Bulgaria, leaving two people dead and 25 missing.
Video released by the Interior Ministry showed only the ship's hull protruding above the surface in rough seas.
The naval authority identified the ship as the Comoros-flagged Khoryv, which the shipping data website MarineTraffic shows departed Turkey on Oct. 21 and was headed for Romania’s Sulina port.
“Rescue teams continue search operations to identify and rescue the other three crew members,” the naval authority said, adding that it wasn't possible to deploy a helicopter due to unfavorable weather conditions and low visibility.
On Saturday, Romanian pilots on air policing duties shot down two drones in Romania’s territorial waters over the Black Sea.

articles.title_orig: SK Hynix Stock Jumps After Scrapping U.S. IPO of Memory-Chip Unit
articles.title_zh: SK Hynix Stock Jumps After Scrapping U.S. IPO of Memory-Chip Unit
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
In July, SK Hynix ( SKHY ) raised $26.5 billion in the biggest US listing ever by a foreign company. Now the company is walking away from one of the biggest tech IPOs ever.
The South Korean memory giant said Friday it has shelved plans to list Solidigm, its flash memory unit, in the US, citing market conditions and share price trends. Solidigm had aimed to raise $10 billion to $15 billion at a valuation of up to $150 billion, according to industry estimates cited by the Wall Street Journal .
For a clue to why, look at the company's own stock.
SK Hynix priced its US shares at $149 in July. SK Hynix stock is rising on Friday but still trades below that price, about a third below the stock's September record.
Memory and storage stocks have shed $1.3 trillion in market value from their 2026 records, according to Yahoo Finance calculations. SK Hynix accounts for about $489 billion of that, and Micron ( MU ) accounts for about $411 billion. Of the 59 chip stocks in a Yahoo Finance basket, 58 are down in October.
That's a strange look for an industry printing money. Memory makers are booking record profits on AI data center demand, and executives see shortages lasting into 2028. The stocks are trading as if the peak is already in, after a $3 trillion chip rout this month.
Solidigm isn't the only AI-linked deal getting pulled back. Australian data center operator Firmus Grid canceled its IPO, and AirTrunk delayed its Singapore listing to next year. OpenAI is now seeking a $1.25 trillion valuation in funding talks , down from $1.4 trillion. Anthropic's ( ANTH.PVT ) blockbuster IPO is expected next month.
The next test for memory stocks comes on Thursday, when Sandisk ( SNDK ) reports after the close.
For SK Hynix, watch $149. A move back above its IPO price would put July's buyers back in the black. Until then, it's a ceiling.

articles.title_zh: 'We're Victims of Xbox's Change in Strategy': Dishonored Dev Has Weeks to Save Itself
articles.content_orig:
Update [ Fri 23rd Oct 2026, 5:30pm ]:
While the future of Arkane Lyon seemed precarious following today’s updates, Bloomberg journalist Jason Schreier has followed up with more positive news.
He says there are “multiple paths being explored” to save the studio and he’d “be surprised if it is shut down”.
He does warn, however, that “anything can happen during negotiations”.
Original Story: While the future of former Xbox first-party devs like Double Fine and Undead Labs has already been determined, it’s been a while since we heard word from Arkane Lyon , the studio behind the acclaimed Dishonored games.
Subscribe to Push Square on YouTube 172k
Now an article by Le Monde (paywalled) gives an insight into the struggles of the French studio, as it races to find a buyer before a 13th November deadline.
As you may recall, Microsoft was unable to close the studio immediately due to a consultation period demanded by French law. The Redmond firm is obligated to try to sell the studio, but a mandated three month deadline is now coming to a close.
The team has until 13th November to find new funding, otherwise the studio will be shuttered and around 217 jobs will be lost. According to the report, negotiations are ongoing.
Union representatives claim the team’s current project, Marvel’s Blade – which was announced in 2023 – is “nearing the end of production”. Spokespeople for the studio believe it will be a success if it sees the light of day.
But those same people blame Microsoft for its “disrespectful” treatment of the team.
“We are collateral victims of Xbox’s change in strategy,” one of the people said.
As alluded to above, Microsoft has already shuttered UK studio Ninja Theory , and offloaded various other teams like Compulsion Games et al.
It’s also in the process of reorganising its entire first-party operations, seemingly sunsetting Xbox Game Studios as it places its remaining teams under the umbrella of Bethesda and Activision. Its objective is to focus on big franchises like Fallout and Call of Duty .
The scary part is that the platform holder is not done yet: it’s cut over 1,800 jobs so far, but more redundancies are coming , as it aims to eliminate 3,200 roles overall.

articles.title_orig: Mystery over source of Ebola infection in Nigeria fuels concern about spread of virus
articles.title_zh: Mystery over source of Ebola infection in Nigeria fuels concern about spread of virus
articles.content_orig:
Switzerland says patient is wife of Swiss diplomat and believed to have contracted virus while travelling in Uganda
Health officials across Africa are racing to determine how Nigeria’s first Ebola patient ⁠in more than a decade ⁠became infected, amid fears ​the outbreak could spread further after reaching a fourth African country.
The Swiss foreign ministry said on Friday the patient in Nigeria, the Ugandan-born wife of a Swiss diplomat based in Abuja, had not travelled to the Democratic Republic of ⁠Congo, where the outbreak was first detected in mid-May before spreading to Uganda , Kenya and now Nigeria. The woman was believed to have contracted Ebola while travelling with her husband in Uganda, the ministry added.
The new information contradicts accounts from Uganda, which previously said the woman had travelled to eastern DR Congo, and will raise concerns about the ability of authorities to contain the outbreak, which is already the most geographically widespread in history.
The Ugandan government reported Ebola cases in May and June before WHO declared it Ebola-free in August. A Ugandan government spokesperson told Reuters on Thursday that Uganda had no ​Ebola cases and that, if ​it did, it would make that information ​public.
The World Health Organization said investigations were continuing to establish the likely source of infection for the Ebola patient in Nigeria.
The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention is investigating whether the patient may have come into contact with an Ebola patient in Kenya, as both travelled from Uganda’s Entebbe airport on 3 October, said Dr Wessam Mankoula, head of emergency preparedness and response at the organisation.
Catherine Smallwood, a WHO Ebola incident manager in DR Congo, told a UN briefing in Geneva via video ‌link on Friday that WHO staff in DR Congo had no information showing the patient in Nigeria had travelled to the country.
Smallwood said a link to the case in Kenya was possible, ​but added that officials would need to compare the timing with when the Nigeria patient’s symptoms began to tell whether the infection more likely happened at the Ugandan airport or elsewhere.
Marion Koopmans, a Dutch virologist and member of the WHO’s Ebola emergency committee, cast doubt on the theory. “I think that is very speculative unless there is evidence of sharing the same ​space in a manner that could explain that,” she said. “Random presence at the same location, a large airport, is not a supported epidemiological link by any standard of what we currently know.”
The Nigerian health minister, Muhammad Ali Pate, said Nigeria’s case remains contained and that contact-tracing was continuing. “We are trying to contain it so it doesn’t go out to the communities. Hopefully, it won’t get to that and we are working hard to ensure that,” Pate said.
Melaku Yirga, vice-president for Africa at Prosper Global (formerly Mercy Corps), said the confirmation of Ebola in Kenya and Nigeria reinforces the need for countries to work closely together to prevent further transmission.
“What matters most now is speed, sharing information across borders without delay and ensuring frontline health workers and local organiaations have the resources to respond quickly,” he said.
Ebola is a highly contagious and often fatal viral disease that affects humans and non-human primates. It spreads through body fluids or contaminated materials and causes organ damage, blood vessel impairment and sometimes severe internal and external bleeding.
The current outbreak is caused by the rare Bundibugyo virus, which has no approved treatment or vaccine. It was first announced on 15 May and has infected more than 9,500 people and killed nearly half of them.
The outbreak is the largest and deadliest in DR Congo’s history and second only ​globally to ​the 2014-16 outbreak in west Africa, which infected ​more than ‌28,600 people ​and ​killed more than 11,000.
Reuters and the Associated Press contributed reporting

articles.content_orig:
While you may think quakes are a western US problem, some of the largest temblors in US history have happened in the East.
PALERMO, Italy — Palermo, the capital of Sicily, and other cities in southern Italy were rocked by a series of earthquakes in the Tyrrhenian Sea on Friday, including a magnitude 5.7 quake, according to USGS.
Italy’s National Institute of Geophysics and Volcanology has recorded nearly three dozen earthquakes, most of them weaker, in the same area of the southern Tyrrhenian Sea north of Sicily.
View of Palermo, Sicily, Italy, Europe.
(Mauro Flamini/REDA/Universal Images Group via Getty Images / Getty Images)
A magnitude 4.9 quake struck just before noon local time Friday, followed by the magnitude 5.7 quake around 12:20 p.m, according to the USGS.
The epicenters of both quakes were about 6 miles below the surface.

articles.title_orig: Volvo Shares Plunge as China Ambitions Fade for Western Carmakers
articles.title_zh: Volvo Shares Plunge as China Ambitions Fade for Western Carmakers
articles.content_orig:
Volvo Cars said Friday it plans to cut 2,500 jobs after a sharp decline in its Chinese market weighed on third-quarter earnings.
The Swedish automaker reported an operating loss of 5.6 billion Swedish kronor ($563.7 million) in the third quarter, down from an operating profit of 6.4 billion Swedish kronor in the previous period.
The company, which is owned by China's Geely Holding, cited a deteriorating environment led by "tougher" market conditions in China and the U.S., which "negatively affected free cash flow."
Volvo Cars shares were 24.2% lower at the end of the trading session.
"It's really a lot about the Chinese market, of course, where the change has come faster than we thought, and really now we can see that selling global cars developed in Europe and China will not work, and then this is affecting all the Western players in China," Volvo Cars CEO Håkan Samuelsson told CNBC on "Squawk Box Europe," on Friday.
Chinese consumers are now looking for "domestic alternatives," which have become stronger and more competitive, the CEO said. "We need a new strategy in China... it has to be a more regional structure, a more empowered region, and we need regionally adapted cars."
He added that costs must be competitive and that Volvo Cars needs to share some platforms with its Chinese parent company Geely, and develop key software in China that includes infotainment and driver-assistance systems. "If you don't have that, I think you cannot sell cars in China."
Volvo Cars' revenues in China fell almost 50% year-on-year as premium brands faced "hypercompetition" from new Chinese rivals, which also put severe pressure on pricing, the company said.
Meanwhile, in the U.S., the automaker cited negative effects from tariffs and fewer customer incentives to buy electric cars, putting pressure on profit margins.
Volvo Cars said it is looking to cut 5 billion Swedish kronor in costs and will eliminate 2,500 jobs globally, with 2,000 of those jobs based in Sweden.
"It is really a consequence of this development, our long-range strategy," Samuelsson told CNBC. "We will have more empowered, stronger regions, and then of course you cannot keep the same resources on the corporate central level. So we need a leaner central administration."

China’s domestic online beauty sales are falling as C-beauty companies are ramping up export efforts and moving into international retail channels. The gap suggests a deliberate pivot from C-beauty toward overseas growth, targeting the categories and regions that K-beauty has spent the past decade winning over.
According to Jefferies’ China online beauty tracker , the country recorded a 6% year-on-year cosmetics sales decline in September 2026. Skin care fell 6.1%, while color cosmetics went down 5.2%.
However, at the same time, data from the Korea International Trade Association (KITA) shows China climbing from seventh place to fifth in global cosmetics exports. The trade body says China’s color cosmetics exports amount to nearly three times that of Korea’s.
C-beauty company Proya, meanwhile, has opened a European Innovation Center Laboratory in France and has announced it will begin selling across 400 Ulta Beauty stores in the US next month.
“This Europe Innovation Center Laboratory connects the European and Chinese ecosystems to draw on combined strengths and create new innovation capabilities,” says Hou Juncheng, founder and chairman of Proya Cosmetics.
The center is not the first bridge between Chinese and European beauty. French ingredient suppliers have been actively pursuing partnerships with Chinese cosmetics brands, and many Chinese perfumers train in France. The country’s Cosmetic Valley, meanwhile, has set up a Shanghai-based fragrance and cosmetics embassy to encourage collaboration between the two markets . Chinese beauty brands are expanding overseas, targeting markets where K-beauty has established a strong presence.
With color cosmetics exports already outpacing Korea’s and a growing foothold in US and European retail, C-beauty appears to be borrowing the playbook that got K-beauty onto global shelves.
The September figures from Jefferies’ tracker show many multinational beauty giants experiencing declining figures in China. L’Oréal fell 5%, Estée Lauder 8%, Procter & Gamble 20%, Shiseido 24%, and LVMH 26%.
Beiersdorf and Galderma were the only multinationals to grow, supported by their Nivea and Cetaphil brands. At the brand level, dermatological skin care like CeraVe and Cetaphil grew (35% and 58%, respectively), while Bobbi Brown fell 31%. Among domestic players, Mao Geping grew 26%, and Proya grew 1%.
As demand becomes increasingly selective, and derma-brands gain ground, Jefferies’ findings show skin care and color cosmetics accounting for over 80% of China’s beauty market. Both categories initially gave rise to K-beauty.
According to KITA, China’s cosmetic exports reached ₩8.14 trillion (US$6.1 billion) from January to July 2026, up 24% from ₩6.55 trillion (US$4.9 billion) a year earlier. The figures lifted China to fifth in global export rankings, behind France in the lead and South Korea in second place.
In color cosmetics, China has already overtaken Korea. Exports of lip and eye makeup, powders, and nail products totaled ₩1.88 trillion (US$1.41 billion) from January to July, about 2.9 times Korea’s ₩644.7 billion (US$484 million).
From January to July 2026, China’s lip makeup exports were 1.7 times Korea’s, and its eye makeup exports were 3.5 times. China’s exports grew 17% to 33% across all four color cosmetics categories (lip, eye, powders, and nail products), while Korea’s lip makeup and nail product exports fell 15% and 15.6%, respectively. Proya is expanding its international presence with a new research laboratory in France.
According to The Asia Business Daily, Kecia Steelman, CEO of Ulta Beauty, raised C-beauty during the company’s 2026 Q2 fiscal earnings call. She is quoted as saying, “[We are launching] Proya, the number one skin care brand in China. So it’s not just about K-Beauty anymore.”
Proya’s US launch will be the first time a Chinese premium skin care brand joins Ulta’s online and physical networks at the same time. The rollout is planned for November this year, and with it, Proya says it is “moving beyond mere product export to brand globalization.”
To expand, the company says, “brands must not only enter overseas markets but also earn a permanent place in consumers’ daily skin care regimens and secure a voice within elite global beauty narratives.”
Securing that voice, Proya has inaugurated its Europe Innovation Center Laboratory in France, with a 450 square meter site containing 76 pieces of equipment and seven dedicated researchers. The lab will focus on research and innovation in skin longevity, biology, biotechnology, and sustainable ingredients.
The lab will collaborate with the Hangzhou Longwu center in China, which handles formulation, ingredients, safety, and efficacy, and the Shanghai center, which works on hair care and the scalp microbiome.
Proya’s international push comes after its namesake brand, which accounts for around 70% of group revenue, posted a 7% sales decline in H1 2026. The drop was the company’s first after years of uninterrupted growth since its 2017 Shanghai listing. Jefferies says the brand returned to 1% growth in September, but the overseas expansion appears partly aimed at offsetting soft momentum.

articles.title_orig: Ukraine hits Russian data centres in blow to Moscow's AI capabilities
articles.title_zh: Ukraine hits Russian data centres in blow to Moscow's AI capabilities
articles.content_orig:
In brief: Drone attacks reportedly damaged infrastructure near Voronezh’s Baltimor airfield, a chemical plant in Perm Krai and a Russian tax service data center in Nizhny Novgorod region. Russian officials reported three injuries and said 443 drones had been downed nationwide.
Ukrainian Drones targeted infrastructure facilities across several Russian regions overnight on Oct. 22-23, with fires reported near the Baltimor military airfield in Voronezh.
Russian officials reported damage to residential buildings and industrial infrastructure, while authorities in Gorodets introduced restrictions following the reported damage to the data center.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
A fire broke out near the Baltimor military airfield in Voronezh following the overnight attack, according to an analysis by the Russian outlet Astra .
An OSINT analyst examined footage provided by eyewitnesses and determined that the fire had occurred in the vicinity of the airfield, with flames and smoke visible.
Voronezh Region Governor Alexander Gusev said dry grass had caught fire due to falling debris.
“Air defense forces on duty detected and destroyed several jet-powered aerial targets in the sky over Voronezh. According to preliminary data, there are no casualties. The fall of debris from the intercepted targets ignited dry grass in the suburbs; the fire has since been extinguished,” he wrote on his Telegram channel.
He added that outbuildings in a garden cooperative (SNT) and several passenger cars sustained damage.
Gusev had earlier warned of a potential missile threat in the region. In the early hours of Oct. 23, he also reported that drone debris had damaged the facade of an apartment building and a passenger car in Voronezh.
Meanwhile, the Ukrainian Telegram channel Exilenova+ reported that, according to preliminary information, the former Voronezh Military Aviation Engineering University and an adjacent military aircraft parking area had been
The university specialized in training military aviation engineers, technicians, and aircraft maintenance specialists. In 2012, it was incorporated into the Zhukovsky and Gagarin Air Force Academy.
“The extent of the damage and potential losses of aviation equipment are currently unknown. We are awaiting confirmation of the results,” the report stated.
According to open-source data, the 47th Guards Bomber Aviation Regiment is stationed at the Baltimor airfield. Since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine on Feb. 24, 2022, the Russian Aerospace Forces have regularly used the airfield to launch airstrikes against Ukrainian territory.
A fire near the Baltimor airfield was previously reported on Sept. 2. Before that, the airfield had been targeted in an attack on May 27.
Monitoring channels reported that the Azot plant in the city of Berezniki, Perm Krai, had been struck. The facility is owned by Uralchem, a company belonging to billionaire Dmitry Mazepin.
Both Astra and Exilenova+ confirmed the reported strike through its own analysis. According to the outlet’s OSINT assessment, smoke was rising from the plant’s premises.
The facility is located nearly 2,000 kilometers (1,243 miles) from the Ukrainian border.
Perm Krai Governor Dmitry Makhonin said on Telegram that air defense forces and mobile fire groups had repelled a drone attack on Friday.
“Twenty drones were shot down in the skies over Perm Krai. Emergency services are working at the sites where the debris fell... An industrial facility sustained minor damage. There are no casualties. Emergency services are on-site,” he wrote.
Makhonin did not identify the industrial facility that had been damaged. He added that the response to the attack had also resulted in minor damage to the windows of two apartments in residential buildings in Berezniki and Solikamsk.
The Azot plant manufactures various chemical products, including nitric acid, ammonium nitrate, and potassium nitrate, which are used, among other things, in the production of gunpowder and explosives .
It is also the only plant in Russia that produces sodium nitrate and crystalline sodium nitrite. Azot was previously targeted in an attack on Sept. 11.
In the city of Gorodets in Nizhny Novgorod region, Ukrainian channels and Astra’s OSINT analysis reported damage to a data center belonging to Russia’s Federal Tax Service.
The facility serves as a backup data center for the tax authority and has been operating since 2015. It was officially opened on Dec. 7, 2015, in a ceremony attended by then-Prime Minister Dmitry Medvedev, Finance Minister Anton Siluanov, and Mikhail Mishustin, who headed the Federal Tax Service at the time and is now Russia’s prime minister.
United Russia, the country’s ruling party, said at the time that the Gorodets facility was part of a three-center system designated as Data Center No. 1. The system also includes the Federal Data Center in Dubna, Moscow region, and Data Center No. 2 in the settlement of Yerzovka in the Volgograd region.
The facilities were designed to back one another up in the event of a failure, helping ensure the “continuity of service provision.”
“Data Center No. 2 provides partial replication of the most critical services in the event of an emergency,” United Russia added.
The centers can store not only tax information but also data from the Unified State Register of Legal Entities (EGRUL), population records – including civil registry (ZAGS) data – cadastral records, and other information.
Municipal authorities in Gorodets and the surrounding district introduced several restrictions following the attack, according to the news outlet NN.ru.
Schools and colleges switched to remote learning, public events were canceled, and traffic across the dam of the Gorky Reservoir was suspended.
Regional Governor Gleb Nikitin acknowledged damage following a drone attack, including damage to “one piece of infrastructure.” He also said three people had been injured “as a result of falling debris.”
Following the reported attack on the Gorodets data center, Mikhail Klimarev, executive director of the Internet Protection Society, suggested on the radio station Echo of Moscow that the consequences could “collapse the entire tax system” and create serious problems for many Russians, who might have to prove their ownership of apartments and land plots.
On the morning of Oct. 23, Russia’s Defense Ministry reported that air defenses had shot down 443 drones over the country. Nizhny Novgorod region and Perm Krai were among the regions listed as having been targeted.
The Ukrainian side has not yet commented on any involvement in the reported attacks.
Julia is a Deputy Head of News and correspondent for Kyiv Post who has previously worked as a parliamentary editor, journalist, and news editor. She has specialized in covering the work of the Ukrainian parliament, government, and law enforcement agencies.

articles.title_zh: People are fixing their TV OSes with Claude
articles.content_orig:

The latest use case for AI? Dumbing down your smart TV to get rid of the bloat. A number of developers and vibe coders have recently been sharing solutions for “vibe-coding” your TV to get rid of sponsored ads, speed up the app launcher, redesign the home screen, disable tracking features, and more.
One such solution, called “dumbtv,” describes its mission on its GitHub page thus: “Your TV should do what you paid for: your apps, your HDMI inputs, and nothing else. No ads from the TV itself, no watch tracking, no update you did not ask for.”
Another, “ cleanyourtv ,” promises to strip the bloatware from any Android TV or Google TV over Wi-Fi, to replace the launcher with one that resembles Apple TV.
While hacking consumer electronics devices to gain more control over their systems is hardly a new idea, the latest advances in AI technology have made such efforts much more accessible to anyone. With smart TVs in particular, the hacks come at a time when people have grown frustrated with being forced to watch ads and put up with their devices surveilling their viewing habits.
Modern smart TVs ship with a technology called automatic content recognition (ACR), which identifies what’s playing on the screen using screenshots, audio clips, or other forms of digital fingerprinting.
If these “dumb TV” hacks become more popular among everyday consumers, they have the potential to disrupt the smart TV ad industry, which profits from selling viewing data to advertisers or using it to display personalized ads on their own interfaces.
As the creator of cleanyourtv, Gathin T., puts it, the idea to clean up the smart TV interface started one afternoon when he got tired of seeing the ads on his parents’ TV set.
Vibe coded my parents' TV this afternoon! It was showing a sponsored ad before you could even get to Netflix. Gave Claude Code the model number, it found the TV on wifi, removed 25 Xiaomi packages and wrote a new launcher. Looks like an Apple TV now lol pic.twitter.com/E5Q4A1b0yI
“I had Claude Code clean it up over Wi-Fi and build a simple home screen with just their apps on it. I put the prompt on GitHub, tweeted the before and after, and a few thousand people did the same to their own TVs over the next two days. Xiaomi, TCL, Sony, Fire TV, LG, a projector or two,” the developer wrote on a website for donations, linked from the project’s homepage .
The solution doesn’t require gaining root access to the TV, nor does it make it impossible to return to the factory default state, if desired.
Meanwhile, the dumbtv solution has been tested end-to-end on a Fire TV Edition television set and Android/Google TV platforms on TVs from Sony, TCL, Philips, Hisense, Xiaomi, and Shield. To use this hack, the developer, Muzzammil Yasin Sabuwala, suggests pointing your preferred AI agent at the dumbtv repository on GitHub.
Sabuwala said he was motivated to work on dumbtv because he was tired of the ads and not being able to delve directly into the content he wanted to watch. His solution was coded using a combination of Deepseek V4.1 Flash, Claude Opus 5.5, and Claude Sonnet 5.5, he told TechCrunch, and he plans to maintain the GitHub, adding support for more models over time.
introducing dumbtv – no spying – no ads from tv – fully customisable to setup just point your agent to this repo – https://t.co/prQLD17Wa4 https://t.co/z41SWJZVXt pic.twitter.com/c6R8EhljiA
Fair warning: All these solutions are works in progress, and various users are now testing them across different TV platforms and suggesting updates and fixes.
However, individuals don’t need to borrow someone else’s work from GitHub to get the job done.
In one newly viral X post, Ryan Doyle explains that he simply sent Claude Code the listing for his TV and asked “Can you hack this?” The agent then talked him through the process, allowing him to remove the ads and bloatware from the TV set, speed up the lagging user interface, and customize his screensaver, he claims.
Doyle then goes on to demonstrate in a video how fast and responsive the new interface is after the AI made the requested changes.
This is how fast the TV moves now that Claude deleted all the BS laggy bloatware it comes with https://t.co/nUCEjqPwAO pic.twitter.com/g07CEgC1GJ
Seeing posts about people “vibe-coding their TVs,” inspired one X user, Mihir Gupta, to try it himself.
“One afternoon with Claude Code: 25 bloat apps disabled, the 192 MB stock launcher replaced with a custom 83 MB one, plus rotating wallpapers,” he wrote .
The end result of these hacks may be mixed, however. Some people have found that Claude wouldn’t respond to their simple suggestions to “hack my TV,” necessitating more complex prompts. Others warned that AI agents could make mistakes, possibly disabling important packages or breaking things in the process. One person even said they bricked their Android TV using Claude , and another got stuck halfway through hacking their Fire TV.
For those wary of using AI to fully hack their TVs, there are existing solutions for customizing Android-based smart TVs, such as home screen replacement apps ATV Launcher, Projectivy Launcher, and FLauncher.

A busy stretch of Interstate 40 East near Raleigh-Durham International Airport reopened Friday morning several hours after Durham police found a woman who was hit by multiple unknown vehicles.
Durham police said they responded to a call about a pedestrian being hit on I-40 near Davis Drive around 1:30 a.m. When they arrived, they found the woman dead and said she had been hit multiple times by unknown vehicles.
The eastbound lanes of I-40 were closed for a mile from Exit 280 at Davis Drive to Exit 281 to South Miami Boulevard. The severe delays extended onto Interstate 885 as well.
At 8 a.m., a lane had reopened on I-40 and traffic was flowing again. All lanes on I-40 reopened by 8:30 a.m.
Hours before the morning commute, WRAL Breaking News Tracker arrived before 4 a.m. to find multiple officers blocking the interstate for an investigation. Police would not let reporters near the scene.
WRAL's Shaun Gallagher arrived at 6 a.m. as the backup worsened. According to Gallagher, the miles of backups on the road resembled 8:30 a.m. rush hour instead of the usual 6 a.m. traffic.
Sky 5 flew over the delays at 7:15 a.m., showing miles and miles of traffic.
Police said they cannot release any other information about the investigation at this time.

articles.title_zh: Ambush of Salvadoran Soldiers Escalates Haiti’s Anti-Gang Mission
articles.content_orig:
El ​Salvador's President Nayib Bukele said Wednesday that Haitian gangs were holding hostage four Salvadoran members of an international UN-backed security force, and that he had launched a ‌military operation to bring them back unharmed.
El Salvador's military and the UN Gang Suppression Force, mandated to help Haitian police fight powerful gangs, earlier this week announced efforts to ​recover the missing Salvadorans, but said intense fighting ​in the area had limited access.
"Today, we have launched a military operation to rescue them," Bukele said in a post on X , ​without providing further details about the operation or identifying ⁠the group holding ⁠the Salvadorans hostage.
The Gang Suppression ‌Force did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The four Salvadorans went missing on Sunday after they leapt from a burning armoured vehicle that was ambushed ⁠by armed gangs on the outskirts of the capital Port-au-Prince while returning from a market to their base, security officials said.
4 soldiers from El Salvador missing in Haiti after attack by gangs
Haitian gangs have ‌cemented their influence over the capital and expanded to surrounding regions over recent years off the back of a longstanding political vacuum, widespread extortion and a flow of illegal arms ​largely from the U.S.
Several nations including Chad and Sri Lanka have deployed soldiers ⁠as part of the Gang Suppression Force, which a year into ⁠its mandate has reached just over a third of its ⁠planned size ⁠and has had limited ​impact on Haiti's security.
Bukele said the missing men were aviation ​technicians, not combatants.
"Our mission ⁠consists only of pilots and technical personnel, whose primary job is to carry out medical evacuations and save lives, not to wage war," he said.
Haiti's government issued a news release Wednesday evening saying the "abduction" of the aviation technicians was an "absolute priority."
It noted that a meeting was held at the prime minister's office "to assess the ongoing interventions and determine the necessary measures to strengthen operations, in close collaboration with the Gang Repression Force."
"The release of the abducted soldiers is an absolute priority, and all necessary resources are being mobilized to achieve this goal," the government said.

articles.title_orig: Ukraine plans independent satellite system as Starlink issues persist
articles.title_zh: Ukraine plans independent satellite system as Starlink issues persist
articles.content_orig:
ICEYE , the European leader in sovereign intelligence from space, and Nokia, a global leader in connectivity infrastructure, today signed a Letter of Intent with the Ministry of Defence of Ukraine, to explore cooperation in space. The partnership aims to support Ukraine’s defense capabilities, particularly in building sovereign satellite communications.
The shared intent was announced on 22 October 2026 during the visit of the Prime Minister of Finland to Ukraine.
Earlier this month, ICEYE and Nokia announced a partnership to develop secure, sovereign and high-performance broadband low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite communications systems for governments, supporting missions from defense and border security to emergency services and disaster response. Built on trusted European technology, the jointly developed satellite communications systems will give nations ownership and control of satellites, ground segment and terminals.
Modern warfare has proven that reliable communications are a matter of national security. We must all rely on capabilities that we can control. The Letter of Intent between the Ministry of Defense, ICEYE, and Nokia is an important step in this direction. I thank Finland and the Prime Minister of Finland for their consistent support. We value partners who not only help Ukraine, but also work with us to build Europe’s long-term security.
Ukraine needs secure, sovereign and high-performance satellite communications systems that it controls. We have a proven track record of delivering sovereign missions at speed to help build that capability. articles.title_orig: Samsung is releasing a new foldable next week, and it just leaked
articles.title_zh: Samsung is releasing a new foldable next week, and it just leaked
articles.content_orig:
The upcoming Samsung W27 could be based on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra and boast the same specifications, but in a more luxurious body and with a more premium asking price
Samsung's ultra-premium, limited-edition W series foldables are offered in the Chinese market. This time, the brand is working on the W27, which could be based on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra.
A recently surfaced image courtesy of Ice Universe on X gives us an early glimpse of the alleged Samsung W27. The leaked photo showcases the foldable smartphone sporting a dark blue finish highlighted by golden accents surrounding the rear camera island.
Talking about specifications, for reference, the Samsung W25 and W26 were just more luxurious aesthetic rebrands of the Galaxy Z Fold 6 Special Edition and Galaxy Z Fold 7 , respectively. The core specs between these devices remained the same. Going by that, we expect the W27 to pack similar specs to the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra .
For starters, it could be powered by the same Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 chipset . The upcoming Samsung foldable may also use the same 200 MP cameras and internal displays, but all in a slightly more luxurious-looking body.
Besides the phone itself, the main selling point of the W series is also its packaging elements. With a custom box, the phone is expected to be offered in its own custom case, power adapter and card of authenticity, which collectors will appreciate.
As for the Samsung W27 pricing, we expect it to be pricier than the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra's Rs 1,99,999 price tag. This is because even the W26 launched at 16,999 Chinese yuan (approx. Rs 2,41,500) in China, which is significantly pricier than the Galaxy Z Fold 7's Rs 1,74,999 price tag in India.
Samsung has yet to announce an official launch date for the W27. However, replying to one of the comments, Ice Universe said the launch date is set for October 29, 2026 . This makes sense since Samsung's previous W series foldables launched in the October to November timeframe.
Another thing to note is that, since Samsung's W series is exclusive to China, we don't really have hopes for it to make it to India.

articles.title_orig: Apple’s $2,000 foldable iPhone hits stores. Is it worth it?
articles.title_zh: Apple’s $2,000 foldable iPhone hits stores. Is it worth it?
articles.content_orig:
Apple’s first foldable iPhone sparked a launch-day circus in New York on Friday, with fans lining up for hours — and in some cases overnight — before stores opened, only to find some flagship locations were already out of walk-in stock by mid-morning.
At Apple’s glass-cube Fifth Avenue store, a video posted online showed a “massive queue” around 4:15 a.m. as customers waited for the new iPhone Duo.
By 10 a.m. , a Reddit user posted that the store had “ran out of stock for walk-ins,” adding that the remaining line was made up of customers with confirmed pickup orders.
The frenzy began well before dawn.
One launch-day customer, Alex Wong, told The US Sun he got in line at 2 p.m. Thursday — a full 18 hours before the Fifth Avenue store’s 8 a.m. opening — and was still only around 25th in line.
Elsewhere in the city, crowds and inventory varied sharply from store to store, underscoring just how uneven Apple’s launch-day supply appeared to be.
At the World Trade Center store, one Reddit user wrote that employees came out at 6 a.m. to start processing orders and that there were “probably 200 people in line.”
The same poster complained: “Many scalpers. Many ordering 2, don’t even know what they’re ordering.”
Another poster at the same location estimated the crowd at “maybe 130 people” and said store staff had warned shoppers there were “very few units” available.
At Apple’s Upper East Side location, a Reddit user summed up the mood more bluntly: “Apple UES NYC — sold out for walk-ins 😓.”
iPhone Duo Apple Store Camp Out in Los Angeles! #iPhoneDuo #Apple pic.twitter.com/LiUbndlwY4
Downtown Brooklyn offered a slightly different picture. One earlier post estimated about 50 people were outside , while another shopper later reported: “WAITED IN LINE, THEY JUST GOT STOCK. ONLY BLUE AS OF 9:18 AM.”
The run on the Duo comes after Apple warned that walk-in quantities at US stores would be limited on launch day.
The social media chatter suggests the scarcity only added to the hype.
In Chicago, one buyer said he arrived 45 minutes before opening and still managed to reserve a 512GB “Night Sky” model.
In Dallas, another said showing up 30 minutes before doors opened was enough to land the configuration he wanted.
An Apple user in Dallas said he waited 11 hours outside Apple’s University Park store to score a white 512GB iPhone Duo.
But in Ardmore, Penn., just outside of Philadelphia, one shopper said he arrived at 5:45 a.m. and the store was “Sold out 7:30ish.”
The same shopper reported that Apple’s King of Prussia, Penn., location sold out shortly after 8 a.m., while nearby Willow Grove Park had also run out by the time he arrived around 9 a.m.
JUST IN – Video shows a massive queue outside Apple Fifth Avenue in New York around 4:15 AM as customers line up for the iPhone Duo. pic.twitter.com/jkLUJyz8mM
He complained about entire families purchasing two phones apiece, including parents who brought babies in strollers and carriers into the chilly morning air.
“[S]calpers suck,” he fumed, adding that he planned to console himself with ice cream while waiting until December for his phone.
At Delaware’s Christiana Mall, another shopper estimated that 200 to 300 people were lined up for the new gadget.
In Orlando, Apple’s store at the Mall at Millenia stopped accepting walk-in orders by about 8:15 a.m., according to a Reddit user who reported that security guards had been stationed throughout the queue and at the cutoff point.
This was the line-before-the-line. 4:15am in Las Vegas (Town Square) with 30-40 people. Now, probably 150+ and I can no longer see the end of the line. pic.twitter.com/r5oeLLo3iw
In Colorado, some would-be customers weren’t even allowed to camp out.
One Reddit user said mall security kicked early shoppers out of Denver’s Cherry Creek location and barred them from lining up until 7 a.m. The customer subsequently headed to another Apple store in Colorado Springs.
Meanwhile, in Las Vegas, a social media user reported that the crowd outside Apple’s Town Square store swelled from an estimated 30 to 40 people at 4:15 a.m. to more than 150 later in the morning.
In Boise, Idaho, a shopper who arrived at 4:45 a.m. said he was 19th in line and managed to purchase a Duo.
The store subsequently sold out, with an estimated 50 to 60 early customers getting phones while later arrivals were turned away.
And in Los Angeles, the launch produced dramatically different outcomes depending on the store.
One shopper at Manhattan Village in Manhattan Beach reported that roughly 50 people lined up and everyone managed to get a phone.
But another Reddit user reported that Apple’s Century City location had already sold out.

articles.title_orig: Excited Apple fans flip out over new iPhone Duo release
articles.title_zh: Excited Apple fans flip out over new iPhone Duo release
articles.content_orig:
By SHIVALI BEST, SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY EDITOR
Published: 04:28 EDT, 23 October 2026 | Updated: 10:34 EDT, 23 October 2026
The iPhone Duo has finally gone on sale today, with shoppers flocking to get their hands on Apple's first foldable.
Photos snapped in London , Bangkok, and Sydney show huge lines outside Apple Stores.
While pre-orders for the £2,000 foldable opened last week, many fans were left disappointed after discovering huge wait times before shipping.
The Daily Mail checked Apple's website, and found that the earliest shipping date for any model is now January 22.
As a result, it seems many desperate fans have taken the good old fashioned approach of visiting an Apple Store to buy the iPhone Duo.
'This is Apple Galaxy Macau. We're still 48 hours from launch time, but there's already a huge crowd,' one user posted on X, alongside a video of a huge queue.
The iPhone Duo has finally gone on sale today, with shoppers flocking to get their hands on Apple's first foldable. Pictured: Sydney
Photos snapped in London, Bangkok, and Sydney show huge lines outside Apple Stores. Pictured: the Covent Garden store this morning
While pre-orders for the £2,000 foldable opened last week, many fans were left disappointed after discovering huge wait times before shipping. Pictured: people wait in line outside the Apple Jing'an Store in Shanghai
Apple announced the iPhone Duo at an event last month, with pre-orders opening at 1pm BST on 16 October.
Storage options : 256GB, 512GB, 1TB, 2TB
Colours : Star White, Night Sky
Outer display : 5.4‑inch Super Retina XDR
Inner display : 7.6–inch Super Retina XDR folding display
Thickness : 11.3mm (folded) / 5.2mm (unfolded)
Battery life : 44 hours using outer display or 31 hours using inner display
Rear cameras : 48MP Fusion Main and 48MP Fusion Ultra Wide
Front/internal camera : 12MP Center Stage camera
However, as eager shoppers flocked to the online Apple Store, stocks quickly dwindled.
Every combination of colour and memory size appeared to be affected by shortages, with no option available before January 22.
'Every variation of the iPhone Duo is sold out until January 2027…..all within 1 hour of pre-orders opening!' one user said.
Another said: 'The iPhone Duo was a disaster; pre-orders are being cancelled, and the website is showing errors, making it impossible to place orders.'
And one vented: 'Worst iPhone pre order day of all time. Good job apple!'
Expected delivery times moved back rapidly as more customers placed their pre-orders.
Early customers reported being offered pre-order times in November or December, while latecomers didn't find any availability until late January.
One customer even complained on X that their expected delivery date had shifted from October 23 to November 9 while they were checking out.
A customer reacts after purchasing Apple's new foldable iPhone Duo at the Apple store in Mumbai, India
People experience the new iPhone Duo at an Apple Store in Taikoo Li on October 23, 2026 in Chengdu, Sichuan Province of China
Park Ha-min, 26, a pre-order customer, celebrates as an Apple Store employee cheers after receiving his new iPhone Duo on its official release day at the Apple Myeongdong store in Seoul, South Korea
The exasperated customer wrote: 'Ordered Apple stuff for years never seen this happen.'
The iPhone Duo comes in just one size, although buyers can choose between four storage options.
The 256GB variant is £1,999/$1,999, while the 512GB variant is £2,199/$2,199 .
At the higher end, the 1TB variant is priced at £2,599/$2,599, while the 2TB variant is £3,199/$3,199.
The iPhone Duo shares the same squat, book-like shape as the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 , meaning the screen is wider than it is tall when opened.
Both the inner and outer screens share the same 1.4 aspect ratio, ensuring that apps don't get distorted or leave dead space when changing between views.
The outer display measures 5.4in, while the inner screen extends out to 7.6in.
Maya Jama took to Instagram to share that she'd managed to get her hands on the iPhone Duo ahead of its release
iPhone resellers holding boxes of iPhone Duo outside an Apple Store on October 22, 2026 in Hong Kong
Users will be able to use the iPhone Duo in any orientation or position, leaving it half open to prop up and watch movies hands-free or holding it partially folded like a book.
Thanks to the new A20 Pro chipset, Apple's new foldable will be able to accommodate multitasking, running different apps on either side of the screen.
Apple says the screen will also support the use of Apple Pencil just like an iPad, making it the first iPhone to do so.
On the back, the iPhone Duo uses the same 48-megapixel camera as the iPhone 18 Pro.
1976 : Founders Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne created the company on April 1, 1976, as they set about selling computer kits to hobbyists, each of which was built by Wozniak.
The first product was the Apple I.
1977 : Apple released the Apple II in June, which was the first PC made for the mass market.
Steve Jobs unveils Apple Computer Corporation's new Macintosh in California on February 6, 1984
1981 : Jobs became chairman.
1984 : The Macintosh was introduced during an ad break for the Super Bowl and later officially unveiled during a launch event. It was discontinued a year later and Jobs left the firm.
1987 : Apple released the Macintosh II, the first colour Mac.
1997 : Apple announces it will acquire NeXT software in a $400 million deal that involves Jobs returning to Apple as interim CEO. He officially took the role in 2000.
Steve Jobs, then-chief executive officer of Apple, with the iPhone
2001 : Apple introduced iTunes, OS X and the first-generation iPod.
The first iPod MP3 music player was released on October 23, 2001, at an event in Cupertino and was able to hold up to 1,000 songs.
2007 : Apple unveils the iPhone.
2010 : The first iPad was unveiled.
2011 : Jobs resigned in 2011 due to illness, handing the CEO title to Tim Cook. Jobs died in October from pancreatic cancer.
2014 : Apple unveiled the Apple Watch. It also unveiled its first larger iPhones - the 6 and 6 Plus.
2015 : After purchasing Beats from Dr Dre, Apple launched Apple Music to compete with Spotify and other music streaming services.
2016 : Apple returned to its roots and announced the 4-inch iPhone SE. Meanwhile, the firm is embroiled in a legal battle with the FBI, involving the agency demanding access to the locked phone used by Syed Farook, who died in a shootout after carrying out a deadly December attack in San Bernardino, California, with his wife. The court order was dropped on March 28 after the FBI said a third party was able to unlock the device.
2017 : Apple introduces the iPhone X, which removes the home button to make way for a futuristic edge-to-edge screen design and a new FaceID system that uses advanced sensors and lasers to unlock phones with just the owner's face.
Jobs at an Apple event at the company's headquarters in Cupertino, California
2018 : In a first for the company, Apple introduces new features in its latest operating system, iOS 12, that encourage users to manage and spend less time on their devices. The move was spawned by a strongly worded letter from shareholders that urged the firm to address the growing problem of smartphone addiction among kids and teenagers.
2019 : In January, Apple reports its first decline in revenues and profits in a decade. CEO Tim Cook partly blamed steep declines in revenue from China.
2020 : In March, Apple closes all its brick-and-mortar retail stores outside of China in response to coronavirus.
2021 : In an online virtual event in April, CEO Tim Cook declares Apple's goal of becoming carbon neutral for Earth Day. Later in the year, the iPhone 13 was announced.
2022 : In September, the iPhone 14 was announced. One of the new features included a new sensor to detect if a user had been in a car crash, as well as an improved camera system.

articles.title_orig: Could Europe’s cost-of-living protests sharpen EU-China trade tensions?
articles.title_zh: Could Europe’s cost-of-living protests sharpen EU-China trade tensions?
articles.content_orig:
Unrest over economic hardship could strengthen calls to protect industry and jobs, though direct impact on trade talks is uncertain
As violent protests fuelled partly by the cost-of-living crisis shake parts of Europe, most notably France, analysts say the unrest could add to pressure on European policymakers to take a tougher trade stance towards China.
“One could argue that the EU looks weaker, but then one could also argue that there is more of a need to show external strength at a time of such events,” said David Henig, director of the UK Trade Policy Project at the European Centre for International Political Economy.
On Thursday, French President Emmanuel Macron said requests to hold protests submitted by people “with no legitimacy” would be banned in the coming days. Requests filed by unions would be examined under the law, while local authorities would propose alternative routes to keep demonstrations away from city centres, he said.

articles.title_orig: What smart people are saying about AI unleashing an online 'vulnerability tsunami'
articles.title_zh: What smart people are saying about AI unleashing an online 'vulnerability tsunami'
articles.content_orig:
It's been a nightmarish week for cybersecurity.
AI helped discover two "critical" flaws in the infrastructure of PHP , a programming language that up to 70% of websites use, prompting companies to race to roll out a fix or risk being hacked.
The incident has illustrated how AI is creating a new level of risk for businesses and consumers online, in a week when multiple other cyber threats caused headaches for security workers.
Here's what executives and analysts are saying about the biggest cyber threat of the moment — and how AI could make things even worse.
Anthropic's deputy security chief, Jason Clinton, warns that a "vulnerability tsunami" is coming — and says critical infrastructure hasn't caught up.
Clinton posted on X on Wednesday about the need to "patch critical infrastructure" before core network vulnerabilities get exploited. On Thursday, he issued another warning to companies.
"As bad as things have gotten in the past 4 days, they are going to get a lot worse before they get better," he wrote.
"Security leaders, never let a crisis go to waste: please go to your boards and ask for help right now. not for ai, for the basics. (we need to hold on for ~18 months.)," he added.
Andrew Curran, a prominent AI analyst, weighed in on several cybersecurity threats from Wednesday to Thursday.
"Regarding potential attacks on energy, food, and water infrastructure, the threat is quite real. Someone is currently probing infra and feeling it out, it is an active threat. Even a little preparation can be helpful, just in case," Curran wrote on Wednesday in response to an NSA cybersecurity advisory about threat actors.
On Thursday, Curran also highlighted a hack of Quest Diagnostics, which he said serves "roughly half" of the US's hospitals and physicians.
In February, Matt Shumer, the former CEO of Hyperwrite, published a viral essay on his website titled "Something Big Is Happening," in which he warned of large-scale disruptions wrought by AI that could upend the world order.
Shumer published another essay on Thursday on his website and LinkedIn, this time titled "The Internet Is Under Attack. Here's How to Protect Yourself and Your Family."
"Right now, as you read this, swarms of AI agents are likely trying to break into the websites you use. Not one of them. Many of them," Shumer wrote. "We are in the middle of the biggest cybersecurity moment in years."
This is what could happen, per Shumer's post:
Shumer also outlined four ways people can protect themselves, including updating all their software and staying off sites they're unfamiliar with while companies and websites alike make their security updates.
He also advises that people protect their bank accounts by being extra cautious about any and all codes and links that they receive. People should also "close the doors you aren't using" by unplugging smart gadgets and deleting apps that aren't being utilized.
"Every connected thing is another way in," Shumer wrote.
Marc Benioff agreed with Anthropic's Jason Clinton in an X post on Thursday.
"Jason is 100% right. Code red," Benioff wrote, along with a red alarm emoji.
Sriram Krishnan, a prominent venture capitalist and former senior AI policy advisor for President Donald Trump, said that the PHP vulnerabilities are a "harbinger of things to come" as AI models continue to detect long-standing cyber issues.
"However the entire software supply chain will need the muscles to rapidly build and deploy fixes," he said in a post on X.
The new cyber reality may require more public-private partnerships to build the required infrastructure, he said.
The Menlo Venture partner Deedy Das warned that "the era of vibe hacking is here" in a series of posts on X.
He said he'd seen firsthand that "even non-technical people" can exploit common vulnerabilities, such as PHP, using AI models. Das said someone could theoretically direct certain models to any website and instruct them to quickly locate the vulnerabilities.
"Once you figure it out, it is downright trivial to do. The digital infrastructure of the world is at risk," he wrote.
AI agents have ended the era of "security through obscurity" because they can devote once-unthinkable time and effort to finding vulnerabilities, Box CEO Aaron Levie said on X. People will need to upgrade legacy infrastructure, modernize security policies, and tighten access controls, among other measures, he said.
"Agents will help on the defensive side because they can both accelerate this work and equally simulate the risk vectors," Levie wrote.
Yet Levie thinks humans also have an important role to play in the cyber revolution — he predicted a boom in cybersecurity jobs , which could become a huge investment area for companies.
"You will need more talent to point the agents at the most critical work, review findings, patch systems, respond to incidents, and more," he said.
